items.title: Anticipa il Black Friday: fino a 500 euro di sconto sui robot Lefant con rullo autopulente ad acqua in tempo reale
items.summary: Corpo compatto, aspirazione da 20.000 Pa e un sistema che lava continuamente il rullo con acqua pulita. M280, M210 Pro Omni e M210 Omni rivoluzionano la pulizia della casa ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Un robot che aspira e lava il pavimento deve riuscire a fare bene entrambe le cose, ma nella vita quotidiana contano anche altri aspetti: arrivare sotto i mobili, non costringere a liberare continuamente le spazzole dai capelli e ridurre il più possibile la manutenzione.

È su queste basi che Lefant ha progettato M280, M210 Pro Omni e M210 Omni, i tre robot protagonisti delle promozioni per il Black Friday del marchio. I modelli condividono buona parte della piattaforma tecnica, ma differiscono per alcune funzionalità e per il livello di prezzo, con offerte che arrivano fino a 178.59 euro. Durante il Black Friday puoi risparmiare fino a 500 euro .

Il punto di partenza comune è un corpo compatto da 280 mm, pensato per muoversi anche negli spazi dove robot più grandi possono fare maggiore fatica.

Ma soprattutto, tutti e tre utilizzano un sistema di lavaggio a rullo che cambia il modo in cui viene gestito lo sporco durante il passaggio.

M280, M210 Pro Omni e M210 Omni utilizzano un rullo da 20 cm che gira a 240 giri al minuto e lavora con una pressione verso il pavimento di 15 N. L'elemento più interessante è il sistema di alimentazione con acqua pulita in tempo reale.

Durante il funzionamento il rullo viene continuamente bagnato, utilizzato per strofinare il pavimento e successivamente raschiato per rimuovere lo sporco raccolto. L'acqua contaminata viene quindi separata invece di continuare a circolare sulla superficie.

Inoltre, il rullo copre l'intera impronta lasciata dalle ruote del robot , così da evitare zone che vengano attraversate senza essere lavate. In questo modo si può effettuare ogni passaggio con una superficie del rullo continuamente ripulita, limitando sia gli aloni sia il rischio di trascinare lo sporco raccolto in una stanza verso quella successiva.

Per l’aspirazione tutti e tre i modelli raggiungono 20.000 Pa , ma Lefant ha scelto di eliminare la tradizionale spazzola a rullo dal canale principale di aspirazione. Al suo posto c'è un ingresso diretto, una soluzione pensata soprattutto per evitare che capelli e peli si avvolgano attorno alla spazzola e debbano poi essere rimossi manualmente.

Nelle case con animali domestici o con persone dai capelli lunghi, l'accumulo attorno agli elementi rotanti è uno dei problemi più frequenti dei robot tradizionali.

I tre robot rinunciano allo svuotamento automatico della polvere nella base. Può sembrare una scelta controcorrente, ma consente di eliminare i sacchetti monouso e il rumore generato dall'aspirazione della polvere dalla macchina alla stazione. Il contenitore presente sul robot è lavabile e viene svuotato direttamente dall’utente.

M280 è il modello più evoluto dei tre. Il rullo di lavaggio non rimane fisso all'interno della sagoma del robot, ma può estendersi lateralmente per avvicinarsi maggiormente a pareti, mobili e angoli . In questo modo viene ridotta la classica striscia di pavimento che alcuni robot tendono a lasciare lungo il perimetro delle stanze.

In presenza di tappeti questo modello mostra ancora di più le sue specificità. Quando M280 ne rileva uno, solleva automaticamente il rullo di 10 mm per evitare di bagnarlo e, contemporaneamente, aumenta la potenza di aspirazione per effettuare una pulizia più profonda della superficie tessile.

Il Lefant M280 è il modello da considerare soprattutto nelle abitazioni con una combinazione di pavimenti duri e tappeti, oppure quando si vuole prestare particolare attenzione alla pulizia lungo pareti e mobili.

Anche il contenitore della polvere è il più capiente dei tre : raggiunge 1 litro ed è trasparente, così da poter controllare facilmente quanto materiale è stato raccolto. Una capacità sufficiente per arrivare fino a 30 giorni prima dello svuotamento.

Per il Black Friday M280 è proposto su Amazon a 349,99 euro invece di 699,99 euro, con uno sconto del 50%. L'offerta è valida fino al 30 novembre.

M210 Pro Omni mantiene la stessa impostazione fondamentale: corpo compatto, aspirazione da 20.000 Pa, ingresso senza spazzola centrale e sistema di lavaggio con rullo alimentato continuamente con acqua pulita.

Rispetto a M280 utilizza un contenitore della polvere da 800 ml, accessibile dalla parte superiore, più che sufficiente per due settimane di utilizzo prima dello svuotamento. Anche in questo caso non sono necessari sacchetti usa e getta .

M210 Pro Omni supporta reti Wi-Fi sia a 2,4 sia a 5 GHz, può essere controllato anche tramite Apple Watch e può gestire fino a tre mappe con suddivisione automatica degli ambienti.

Queste opzioni di connettività lo rendono una soluzione particolarmente adatta alle abitazioni su più livelli: invece di ricostruire ogni volta l'ambiente, il robot può conservare differenti mappe della casa.

Durante la promozione Black Friday su Amazon il prezzo scende inizialmente a 239,99 euro ma applicando il codice XGOR07PO si ottiene un ulteriore 17% di sconto: il prezzo finale scende così a 199.19 euro. La promozione è valida fino al 30 novembre.

M210 Omni è invece il punto d'ingresso della famiglia. La caratteristica che lo distingue maggiormente è lo spessore di appena 85 mm . È il robot con lavaggio a rullo più sottile sul mercato. Ma non si tratta solo della scheda tecnica; è una specifica molto concreta perché è pensata per sfruttare il vantaggio del corpo compatto quando bisogna raggiungere lo spazio sotto divani, letti e mobili particolarmente bassi.

Anche qui è integrato un contenitore superiore da 800 ml, con una capacità dichiarata sufficiente per contenere fino a circa due settimane di sporco. Non serve acquistare sacchetti e viene mantenuta la scelta di evitare lo svuotamento automatico tramite la base.

Rimangono anche le caratteristiche fondamentali condivise con i fratelli maggiori: 20.000 Pa di aspirazione, ingresso diretto anti-groviglio e il rullo da 20 cm che si pulisce continuamente con acqua fresca durante il lavaggio.

È il modello pensato per chi vuole soprattutto queste caratteristiche senza le funzionalità aggiuntive del M210 Pro Omni o il rullo estensibile e sollevabile di M280.

Anche il prezzo è il più basso dei tre. Su Amazon M210 Omni parte da un listino di 599,99 euro e viene proposto in anticipo per il Black Friday a 189,99 euro. Utilizzando il codice C8NB78OH si ottiene un ulteriore sconto del 6%, arrivando così a 178.59 euro. La promozione è valida fino al 30 novembre.

La tecnologia di base rende i tre robot molto vicini tra loro. Tutti puntano su dimensioni compatte, aspirazione senza spazzola centrale e un sistema di lavaggio che continua a ripulire il rullo mentre il robot si muove.

Sono tre interpretazioni diverse della stessa piattaforma, con un elemento comune che rimane al centro dell'esperienza: lavare il pavimento con un rullo che viene pulito continuamente durante il lavoro, anziché occuparsene soltanto quando il robot ritorna alla base.

items.title: Oggi lo sciopero, in piazza lavoratori e studenti. Cgil: 'La manovra va cambiata'
items.summary: Manifestazioni in oltre 100 piazze. Attesi i big del campo largo. Mobilitazione degli studenti, in piazza anche i Cobas
items.content:
Giornata di protesta, con lavoratori e studenti in piazza, e disagi in vista. La Cgil si prepara allo sciopero generale, il quinto di fila contro la manovra del governo Meloni, chiedendo risposte e dicendo basta alla "propaganda".

Attesi in piazza anche i big del campo largo: la segretaria del Pd Elly Schlein, il presidente M5s Giuseppe Conte, il leader di Avs Nicola Fratoianni. Quello di oggi è un appuntamento a doppio filo: il sindacato sceglie di abbracciare la mobilitazione studentesca, che vedrà i giovani sfilare nelle città italiane ed europee. In una giornata che conta anche lo sciopero generale indetto dai Cobas. Proteste separate e posizioni diverse. Sul banco degli imputati, la legge di Bilancio e il carovita, lo sguardo al futuro del Paese. La Cgil scende in cento piazze contro una manovra che "accelera il declino e l'impoverimento dell'Italia". E che quindi, insiste, va cambiata.

"Quando abbiamo detto che non va bene, ci hanno accusato di essere pregiudiziali. Ma i duemila emendamenti presentati dalla maggioranza dimostrano come i primi a non essere convinti di aver fatto una legge buona per il Paese sono loro...", attacca il segretario generale della Cgil, Maurizio Landini.

Allo stesso modo respinge ancora una volta le critiche per aver proclamato un altro sciopero di venerdì: "Quando una persona decide di aderire ad uno sciopero non lo fa per fare un ponte, ma per portare a casa risultati e per migliorare i diritti anche degli altri e rinuncia al proprio stipendio". Non riconoscere questo "è disprezzo". Lo sciopero generale è di 24 ore e interessa tutti i settori pubblici e privati: dalla scuola alla sanità fino al trasporto pubblico locale (stop con fasce di garanzia per bus e metro), dai porti ai taxi.

Esclusi dall'astensione, dopo l'intervento del Garante, invece il trasporto aereo, ferroviario e il trasporto merci su rotaia. Ma per i treni dalle 21 di oggi e fino alle 20 di domani scatterà un altro sciopero, indetto dai sindacati Sgb (Sindacato generale di base) e Cub trasporti.

Landini oggi sarà al corteo a Roma: "Mi aspetto piazze piene, molto partecipate e colorate. Sarà una bellissima giornata", al fianco degli studenti, per difendere i diritti di oggi e domani: "Il futuro è adesso", è del resto lo slogan scelto. Sul tavolo la richiesta di aumentare i salari e le pensioni, di contrastare il carovita, di investire sulla scuola e sulla sanità pubblica, di fare politiche industriali mirate e una vera riforma fiscale "per andare a prendere i soldi dove sono":

introducendo un contributo di solidarietà sui super ricchi - la proposta richiama la patrimoniale - e fermando il drenaggio fiscale. E dire no al riarmo. Sui salari replica la ministra del Lavoro, Marina Calderone: "Rispetto" lo sciopero, premette, "però credo che il governo abbia dato e stia dando delle risposte".

In piazza scendono anche i Cobas, contro il caro-vita e l'economia di guerra, per gli investimenti sul sociale e la reintroduzione di meccanismi automatici che garantiscano il pieno adeguamento di retribuzioni e pensioni all'inflazione reale, ma anche contro l'accordo tra Cgil, Cisl e Uil e tredici associazioni datoriali che "nel lavoro privato toglierebbe ai sindacati di base ulteriormente diritti".

Non scioperano Cisl e Uil, che invece hanno deciso altre forme di mobilitazione: il sindacato guidato da Daniela Fumarola con tre manifestazioni sotto lo slogan "Il Patto che unisce", dopo la prima tappa di Genova sarà il 28 novembre a Gioia Tauro e poi il 12 dicembre a Roma per la manifestazione nazionale. La Uil di Pierpaolo Bombardieri è in campo con venti iniziative di mobilitazione a livello regionale, sia per chiedere modifiche sulla manovra sia per sollecitare le regioni e i comuni a ridurre il peso della tassazione locale.

Lavoratori e studenti in piazza e oltre cento manifestazioni in tutta Italia: sono due gli scioperi generali proclamati per domani - uno dalla Cgil e l'altro dai Cobas - a cui si affianca la mobilitazione studentesca, organizzata a livello europeo. Lo sciopero generale è di 24 ore e interessa tutti i settori pubblici e privati : dalla scuola alla sanità fino al trasporto pubblico locale, dai porti ai taxi. Lo stop per autobus, tram e metro sarà nel rispetto delle fasce di garanzia stabilite a livello locale e vedrà alcune aziende escluse . Esclusi dall'astensione , dopo l'intervento della Commissione di garanzia, invece il trasporto aereo, ferroviario e il trasporto merci su rotaia . Ma per i treni dalle 21 di domani scatterà un altro sciopero , indetto dai sindacati Sgb (Sindacato generale di base) e Cub trasporti. Molte le manifestazioni previste: a quelle della Cgil (circa 100 in tutto il Paese) si aggiungono quelle dei Cobas (una quarantina) e degli studenti in tutta Italia.

VOLI E TRENI. Niente stop, dunque, per i voli. Mentre il trasporto ferroviario in parte resta a rischio: l'altro sciopero dei sindacati di base va dalle 21 di venerdì 20 fino alle 20 di sabato 21 novembre.

TRASPORTO PUBBLICO LOCALE. Escluse dallo sciopero alcune aziende Tpl in alcune città, come Atm a Milano, Atvo a Venezia, Anm a Napoli e Amtab a Bari. Per il resto stop di 24 ore per bus, tram e metro, nel rispetto delle fasce di garanzia: a Torino stop dalle 9 alle 12 e dalle 15 a fine servizio; a Genova dalle 9 alle 17.30 e dalle 20.30 a fine servizio; a Bologna dalle 8.30 alle dalle 16.30 e dalle 19.30 a fine servizio; a Firenze dalle 8.15 alle 12.30 e dalle 14.30 a fine servizio; a Roma dalle 8.30 alle 17 e dalle 20 a fine servizio; a Palermo dalle 8.30 alle 17.30 e dalle 20.30 a fine servizio.

TAXI E PORTI. Anche per i taxi sciopero di 24 ore, articolato all'interno dei turni e garantendo i servizi minimi. Nel trasporto marittimo, per i collegamenti con le isole maggiori ritardi di 24 ore alla partenza della nave; per i collegamenti con le isole minori sciopero dalle 00.01 alle 24 (in entrami i casi ad esclusione di linee e servizi essenziali). Incrociano le braccia per l'intera giornata anche i lavoratori del trasporto merci e logistica e gli addetti alla viabilità di autostrade e Anas (garantiti i servizi minimi funzionali ad assicurare la sicurezza della circolazione stradale).

LE PIAZZE. Sono circa 100 le manifestazioni organizzate dalla Cgil in tutto il Paese a sostegno della protesta contro la manovra: il segretario generale Maurizio Landini sarà a Roma, al corteo che partirà alle ore 9.30 da piazza Vittorio Emanuele II per sfilare verso via dei Fori Imperiali. I Cobas scenderanno in piazza con oltre 40 manifestazioni territoriali: nella capitale il corteo partirà alle 9.30 da piazzale Aldo Moro verso il ministero dell'Istruzione in viale Trastevere. Decine anche i cortei organizzati dagli studenti da nord a sud: a Roma sfileranno dalle 9.30 da Porta San Paolo verso piazza del Colosseo/via Cavour.

items.title: Attacco su Kiev, tre morti e colpiti i ponti cittadini
items.summary: Traffico interrotto. Incendi in tre quartieri
items.content:
Tre persone sono rimaste uccise e due ferite in un attacco missilistico condotto dalle truppe russe su Kiev nella notte, e alcuni ponti della capitale sono stati danneggiati. Lo rendono noto le autorità cittadine. "A seguito di un attacco balistico sulla capitale, si sono verificati danni al ponte Podils'ko-Voskresenskyi. Attualmente, il traffico da una sponda all'altra è interrotto. Sono stati rilevati anche danni al ponte Darnyts'kyi. Gli specialisti potranno valutare l'entità dei danni alle infrastrutture una volta terminata l'allerta aerea. Un altro impatto si è verificato sul Ponte Meridionale". Lo scrive su Telegram il sindaco di Kiev Vitaliy Klitschko.

"A causa delle difficoltà di traffico tra le due sponde della capitale, chiedo ai residenti di evitare di utilizzare l'auto privata per recarsi in città, se non strettamente necessario" scrive ancora il sindaco di Kiev. "Inoltre - aggiunge - invito le istituzioni e le aziende che ne hanno la possibilità a implementare un sistema di lavoro da remoto per i propri dipendenti. L'attacco missilistico del nemico a Kiev è in corso.

Tutti i servizi stanno facendo e continueranno a fare tutto il possibile per risolvere il più rapidamente possibile le conseguenze dell'attacco".

Inoltre si sono verificati incendi in più zone di Kiev. Lo ha riferito l'amministrazione militare di Kiev, secondo quanto riportato da Ukrinform. "Secondo le prime informazioni, un incendio è scoppiato in un edificio di tre piani nel quartiere di Obolon a seguito di un attacco nemico", si legge nel comunicato. Inoltre è stato registrato un incendio in un edificio nel distretto di Podilskyi. Più tardi il sindaco di Kiev Vitali Klitschko, e l'amministrazione militare della città di Kiev hanno riferito con più dettagli di incendi e danni in almeno tre distretti a causa di un attacco missilistico russo nella notte: Obolonskyi, Podilskyi e Holosiivskyi le zone colpite. Nel distretto di Obolonskyi, la caduta di detriti di un missile ha provocato un incendio in un edificio di tre piani, ha reso noto Klitschko. Nel distretto di Podilskyi, a seguito dell'attacco, ha preso fuoco un edificio situato in un'area non residenziale. Il sindaco ha inoltre segnalato un impatto in uno spazio aperto vicino a uno dei ponti di Kiev. L'entità di eventuali danni alle infrastrutture circostanti non è stata ancora determinata. Nel distretto di Holosiivskyi, un colpo ha colpito l'area di una struttura infrastrutturale; secondo le prime informazioni, un edificio adibito a uffici all'interno del complesso ha preso fuoco. Il bilancio delle vittime è arrivato nella prima mattina: "Purtroppo, tre persone sono morte a seguito dell'attacco nemico alla capitale", si legge nel rapporto dell'amministrazione militare della città.

items.title: Putin apre il tavolo agli europei. Trump li chiama, 'basta soldi a Kiev'
items.summary: Meloni con i Volenterosi: 'Mandato chiaro all'E5'. Zelensky: 'Garanzia è l'adesione Nato'
items.content:
Prima l'invito di Vladimir Putin, che vorrebbe ricevere gli europei a Mosca per "comprendere la loro posizione". Poi la telefonata di Donald Trump dall'Air Force One, di ritorno dalla Cina, per assicurare che il colloquio con il presidente russo è andato "bene" e che "contribuirà a favorire la pace in Ucraina".

Rassicurazioni, secondo Politico Germania e Welt, accompagnate da una critica all'Ue per aver fornito altri miliardi di aiuti all'Ucraina. Visti i precedenti, gli europei prendono ovviamente con tutte le cautele del caso i segnali che arrivano a Berlino mentre gli oltre trenta Paesi della Coalizione dei Volenterosi sono riuniti con Volodymr Zelensky e i due inviati speciali Usa, sotto la guida degli E3 (Francia, Germania e Gran Bretagna), e con al debutto l'altro formato E5, allargato a Italia e Polonia, incaricato di parlare a nome dell'Europa.

Le diplomazie prendono atto che Washington vuole accelerare il processo negoziale per arrivare alla fine della guerra in Ucraina, c'è un'inerzia che viene ritenuta "particolarmente favorevole", come spiegano fonti italiane.

Per questo i consiglieri di sicurezza degli E5 e dell'Ucraina con gli inviati Usa, Kushner e Steve Witkoff, si fermano a lavorare in Cancelleria dopo la fine del vertice dei leader, preceduto da una riunione ristretta degli E3, che proseguono sulla strada della Forza multinazionale e sono impegnati in questi giorni nella prima esercitazione congiunta. Alla fine, nella conferenza stampa degli E3 con Zelensky e gli americani, lo scetticismo si intreccia con le strategie. Emerge anche dalle parole di Giorgia Meloni ("Francamente, non so cosa aspettarmi dai russi"), che davanti ai leader esorta Pechino a "usare la sua influenza" su Mosca.

La premier a un certo punto sembra intenzionata a lasciare con un'ora di anticipo i lavori per dedicarsi a una riunione di maggioranza sulla manovra, poi rimane fino al termine. E nel suo intervento chiede anche un "mandato chiaro" all'E5: "Cosa chiediamo, cosa offriamo e cosa non accetteremo mai". Per gli analisti, a Berlino va in scena un controvertice rispetto a quello di Shenzen, che Friedrich Merz liquida come una "photo opportunity", e che per Emmanuel Macron non porta certo "a una riorganizzazione del mondo".

"Siamo pronti a parlare con Putin ma in un luogo neutrale", è la linea esplicitata dal cancelliere tedesco, che agli ospiti regala un frammento del Muro di Berlino e mutua il suo appello a Putin da quello di Reagan a Gorbaciov a "tirare giù il muro": "Metta fine a questa guerra e lasci che si trovi una soluzione diplomatica". E comunque "un formato Yalta non servirà alla pace", puntualizza stigmatizzando l'idea di colloqui segreti fra superpotenze sulla testa dell'Ucraina.

È da verificare anche se ora Usa ed europei hanno una posizione sull'Ucraina "molto più vicina", come garantisce Kushner, spiegando che Trump è aperto ad estendere a Kiev la clausola Nato di mutua difesa, la cui idea è rivendicata da Giorgia Meloni. Macron va oltre: "Serve riaprire la questione dell'adesione dell'Ucraina all'Alleanza atlantica". E chiarisce il "giusto ordine" in cui affrontare i nodi del negoziato: garanzie di sicurezza, territori e solo dopo la pace.

Per Zelensky l'adesione alla Nato sarebbe la "migliore garanzia di sicurezza" per il suo Paese. Intanto accoglie il sostegno finanziario da 45 miliardi dell'Ue e chiede altri aiuti militari. E il presidente francese fa appello agli alleati della coalizione: "Tutti devono fare il massimo per fornire all'Ucraina le capacità di cui ha bisogno per resistere". Anche se il britannico Andy Burnham nota che "il perdente più grande è probabilmente la Russia: ha perso in tre mesi tanti uomini quanti nei nove anni complessivi della guerra in Afghanistan".

"Putin si è atteggiato a leader globale a Shenzhen. In realtà, è un criminale e terrorista globale. E dovrebbe essere trattato come tale. Esprimiamo la nostra piena solidarietà ai nostri colleghi austriaci e chiediamo una forte risposta internazionale agli attacchi brutali della Russia". Lo afferma su X il ministro degli Esteri ucraino Andrii Sybiha, dopo i raid con droni russi vicino all'ambasciata d'Austria e a quella di Paesi Bassi a Kiev. Attacchi che hanno provocato almeno un morto.

items.title: Driver NVIDIA, segnalate scritture anomale sugli SSD
items.summary: Le segnalazioni riguardano i driver GeForce 621.14 e 621.24.
items.content:
Decine di gigabyte scritti sull'SSD senza aprire un gioco o spostare un file. È quello che alcuni utenti GeForce hanno notato dopo aver aggiornato i driver NVIDIA alle versioni 621.14 e 621.24, entrambe distribuite a novembre.

Al netto della problematica, i numeri cambiano parecchio a seconda del PC, ma nelle segnalazioni raccolte da TroubleGrid e riprese da TechSpot c'è chi vede poche decine di megabyte e chi parla di decine di gigabyte al giorno. NVIDIA al momento della pubblicazione non ha ancora confermato il problema, ma cerchiamo di capire cosa è successo.

A scrivere sul disco sarebbe NVDisplay.Container.exe, un processo che resta attivo in background e tiene un registro della propria attività. Il sospetto è che con questi driver il processo riscriva il registro intero invece di aggiungere le nuove righe in fondo. Un file da pochi megabyte può quindi restare più o meno della stessa dimensione e generare comunque molte più scritture di quanto ci si aspetterebbe.

items.title: Apple annuncia il Black Friday 2026: Gift Card fino a 240 euro e periodo di reso esteso
items.summary: Per il Black Friday Apple ha deciso di puntare ancora una volta sulle Gift Card
items.content:
Per il Black Friday Apple ha deciso di puntare ancora una volta sulle Gift Card. Dal 27 al 30 novembre sarà possibile ottenere fino a 240 euro in carte regalo acquistando uno dei prodotti selezionati. Come già accaduto negli anni scorsi, Apple non ridurrà direttamente i prezzi: le Gift Card potranno essere spese in seguito. La promozione sarà valida sia negli Apple Store fisici sia online, anche attraverso l'app Apple Store.

Per gli acquisti natalizi ci sarà anche più tempo per cambiare idea: il termine per effettuare i resi è stato spostato al 20 gennaio 2027. Restano poi disponibili il programma di permuta Apple Trade In, i finanziamenti e il supporto degli Specialist per scegliere e configurare i dispositivi.

QUALI GIFT CARD SI POSSONO OTTENERE

Si parte venerdì 27 novembre e si chiude lunedì 30. Le Gift Card non sono previste per tutta la gamma Apple, ma solo per determinati prodotti, fino a esaurimento scorte. Il valore della Gift Card cambia a seconda del prodotto acquistato, con il massimo di 240 euro previsto per alcuni Mac.

items.title: Jujutsu Primer
items.summary: Article URL: https://ethanlowman.com/posts/jj-primer/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50570628 Points: 21 # Comments: 6
items.content:
This guide is a brief(ish) introduction to the Jujutsu ( jj ) version control system (VCS) for someone familiar with Git.

jj provides primitives for version control that are simple to learn, but elegantly compose into powerful workflows. Features like automatic rebase and native undo soften the sharp edges of Git. Eventually, you’ll organically discover new powerful workflows that would be too cumbersome to attempt with most other VCS tools.

If you work in a Git repository, you can try it today. Jujutsu and Git can be used side-by-side in the same repository , so you can try out jj on a git repo on your own, without fully ejecting from git .

Personally, I think jj considerably boosts my effectiveness, because it allows me to keep VCS bookkeeping out of my working memory. Automatic rebasing also makes stacked diff workflows quite easy, and reduces thrashing of my working memory. It’s also just a fun tool to use.

Official installation instructions are here , but here are a few common methods:

From here on, jj and git repo state will be synchronized automatically.

You can edit jj ’s TOML configuration for your user in an editor with:

In addition to the --user scope, jj config also has --repo and --workspace scopes. View the merged config with:

A commit , also called a revision , is essentially the same thing as a git commit. It represents a snapshot of repository state that descends from one or more parent repository snapshots. It is often visualized as a diff against a singular parent commit, or in the case of a merge commit, the diff against multiple parent commits once merged.

When using a Git repo backend, the jj commit ID is the same as the git commit ID: a hash formatted as a hex string. In the output of jj log below, the hex hashes 2bea5e3d and 849165bc on the right are commit IDs.

The IDs on the left hand side ( royxmykx and kpqxywon ) are change IDs , which are stable identifiers for logical changes as they physically evolve over time. We’ll discuss these more in the next section.

Commit IDs and change IDs can be referenced in shorthand with an unambiguous (unique) prefix. jj helpfully highlights the shortest unique prefix of most IDs to make it easy to type them manually. For example, instead of copying and pasting kpqxywon , we can type in a prefix, down to the shortest unique prefix k .

We can inspect the commit 2bea5e3d with jj show , using its short prefix 2 .

Many folks configure a custom diff formatter, like Delta . See configuration docs if you’re interested.

On commit 849165bc , you’ll see the symbol @ on the graph node. This represents a snapshot of our working copy , or the code we have actually checked out in our local directory. We can inspect this special commit pointer in a variety of ways:

jj show shows commit details and a diff, which is empty here. $ jj show Commit ID: 849165bca19639dbd6ccb53e8c1340e78c36d59a Change ID: kpqxywonksrltlrkyqukqqsxpltznztk Author : Ethan Lowman ethan@example.com > ( 2026-11-15 12:17:12 ) Committer: Ethan Lowman ethan@example.com > ( 2026-11-15 12:17:12 ) (no description set)

jj status shows repo state with diff stats. $ jj status The working copy has no changes. Working copy (@) : k pqxywon 8 49165bc (empty) (no description set) Parent commit (@-): r oyxmykx 2 bea5e3d main | Adjust config

jj diff works much like git diff . Its output is empty here, since there are no changes in the current working copy relative to the parent commit.

This output isn’t very interesting, since @ has no changes. Let’s make an example change to see what happens. If we edit main.py and rerun jj show , we see this:

You’ll notice several things have changed. The working copy has been automatically committed, and @ is no longer marked (empty) . The new commit ID for @ is 66b59f20 , since we’ve added changes, but the change ID for 66b59f20 is still kpqxywon . jj has no staging area like in git , so we don’t have to manually add files. When we run a jj command to inspect or modify repo state after editing files, jj automatically snapshots the working copy as a new physical commit for the relevant logical change.

Let’s give this change a description (also called a commit message). We can either run jj desc , which opens an editor, or provide it directly with -m .

Notice again that the commit ID has changed, since the hash covers the commit message, but the change ID has remained stable.

Now, let’s say we’re ready to use this new feature, and we want to organize that change in a separate commit. We can create a new commit with jj new :

We’ve created an empty change nlrtlrxv on top of kpqxywon . jj status reflects that we are editing this new revision which does not yet differ from its parent.

jj commit is a shorthand for this common jj desc and jj new combo. Let’s make another change to use our new feature, and commit it.

To inspect the commit we just created ( n ), we can no longer use the bare jj show , which defaults to showing @ . We have to pass the revision we want to inspect:

We can describe empty commits to record intent before starting work. Let’s create a new commit on top of k to remind ourselves that we need to document the feature.

A separate jj desc would also work just fine instead of the -m flag on jj new . Here’s the current commit graph:

Note how we’ve created branching commits without creating a named branch. This highlights a major difference between jj ’s branchless model and git ’s branch-centric model of organizing work streams. Instead of juggling your work-in-progress on branches, you work on a graph of commits. Once ready to share, you push branches to a Git forge from your commit graph (more on that later).

A revset, an idea borrowed from Mercurial, is an expression that selects a set of revisions from the commit graph. Most jj commands accept revsets in their arguments. When we ran jj new k , the argument k was actually a trivial revset that resolved to the single change with ID kpqxywon . The jj log command has an -r flag that we can use to preview a revset. Some demonstrative examples follow.

Commits authored by ethan@example.com that also have ID k or q :

I’ll defer to the official documentation for exhaustive detail. The Revsets language specification is easily my most referenced jj documentation page, so I would recommend skimming it to see what’s possible.

Let’s say in the course of documenting our feature in qwyusntz we realized we made a mistake in the implementation in parent change kpqxywon . We don’t need to manually commit or stash changes to switch tasks. We simply switch our working copy to kpqxywon with jj edit :

Our working copy once again shows the changes from kpqxywon .

jj hasn’t lost track of the changes above our working copy, including our most recent edits to q :

Instead of switching commits with jj edit k , we could have run jj edit @- . The revset @- is evaluated before switching the working copy, so this moves to the parent commit. The built-in commands jj next [--edit] and jj prev [--edit] provide another way to move up and down a stack of commits.

If we edit files in the working copy, the descendant commits will be automatically rebased upon the next jj invocation. For example, if we edit my_new_feature ’s implementation in main.py and then run jj log , we’ll see that changes k , n , and q all get new commit IDs. jj also tells us that it performed a rebase.

If the automatic rebase happened to cause merge conflicts, jj doesn’t require us to fix them immediately, like git rebase would. Instead, jj records that the commit is conflicted and lets you carry on with your current task. This is massively helpful to reduce mental context switching, as your stacked commits grow more complex.

In a text editor, we can resolve these conflicts, and the next time we run any jj command, we’ll see that jj has marked the commit as unconflicted:

Let’s say we made a mistake in that conflict resolution, and we want to undo it. In git , undoing an action, if it’s even possible, is often complicated. In jj , we can always run jj undo :

More generally, jj maintains a history of all actions in jj op log . We can inspect this log and jj op restore to a point in that history, or jj op revert an individual operation. If the jj undo itself was a mistake, we can jj redo .

The Hint in the output above is a bit of a spoiler for our next topic, the squash workflow.

Editing commits that have descendants can sometimes feel sketchy. If you’re iterating on a large diff that has left your working memory, it would be nice to separate your new changes from the existing diff. For example, we might like to inspect the diff that resolves a rebase conflict in isolation.

Let’s follow the instructions from the above output. We first create a new commit on top of the conflicted commit:

Now we can resolve the conflicts in main.py in our editor, and rerun jj log :

We can inspect the diff in @ if we like, and when we’re happy with the conflict resolution, we can squash it into the parent commit:

One of the powerful qualities of jj is that it makes diffs malleable like clay. With automatic rebase and the confidence inspired by jj undo , we can move, combine, drop, and split diffs with ease.

items.title: Canva ora permette di nascondere le funzioni di AI generativa
items.summary: Due nuove opzioni, anche per chi usa il piano gratuito.
items.content:
Chi usa Canva soprattutto per impaginare presentazioni o preparare una locandina può ora nascondere gli strumenti che generano immagini, testi e altri contenuti. Canva ha aggiunto due impostazioni agli account Free e Pro, perfette per coloro che proprio non vogliono avere a che fare con i tool generativi, o con l'AI in generale.

La prima agisce sui comandi che si vedono nell'editor e nel resto del servizio, mentre la seconda riduce il numero di modelli ed elementi generati dall'AI che compaiono quando si cerca qualcosa nella libreria. Entrambe sono gratuite e si possono cambiare in qualsiasi momento.

Per la prima impostazione si parte dal profilo, si entra in Impostazioni e si apre la sezione Autorizzazioni. Da lì si può spegnere l'interruttore delle funzioni di AI generativa. Restano disponibili strumenti come Background Remover, che ritaglia il soggetto di una foto, e Magic Grab, che permette di spostare un oggetto già presente nell'immagine, diciamo dunque che non è un'eliminazione totale. Questo perché Canva li considera strumenti di modifica e il loro utilizzo, da solo, non fa scattare l'etichetta di contenuto generato con l'AI nei metadati del progetto.

Il miglior top gamma Android? Oppo Find X9 Pro, compralo al miglior prezzo da Amazon Marketplace a 1,175 euro.

items.title: One UI 9.5, il meteo Samsung potrebbe anticipare i viaggi
items.summary: Nella beta per Galaxy S26 spunta una funzione che suggerisce il meteo della destinazione.
items.content:
L'app Meteo dei Galaxy potrebbe mostrare le previsioni per la città in cui stiamo per andare, prima ancora di partire. SamMobile ha trovato la funzione in una versione beta di One UI 9.5 per i Galaxy S26. Quando il telefono riconoscerà un viaggio in programma, l'app suggerirà di dare un'occhiata al meteo della destinazione. Basterà toccare il pulsante nella scheda per aprire le previsioni locali, senza dover cercare e aggiungere la città a mano.

L'idea è sfruttare informazioni che il telefono può già avere. Secondo SamMobile, a metterle insieme sarebbe Personal Agent Core, un sistema in sviluppo che ricava il contesto da diverse app Samsung e Google.

Indubbiamente utile in molte situazioni, pensiamo ad esempio un appuntamento in un'altra città o un volo in programma,, e sono solo due esempi di informazioni che potrebbero far comparire il suggerimento. L'app Meteo si occuperebbe quindi di mostrare le previsioni della località individuata, mentre il sistema che riconosce il viaggio lavorerebbe a monte.

items.title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged
items.summary: African countries at the UN climate summit in Turkey are demanding more funding from developed nations to help them cope with climate change.
items.content:
In Uganda's northern Karamoja region, Elijah Lobur and his family now eat just one meal a day.

A severe drought that began in April has destroyed crops, while food brought in from elsewhere has become increasingly unaffordable.

"Seven months without rain has brought us to this point where we now live in hunger," the 44-year-old farmer, who lives with his grandmother, wife and five children, told the BBC.

"Even some of the wild plants that we used to eat have withered and dried up."

Local officials say more than 90% of crops have failed in the region, where agriculture is largely rain-fed.

Further south, in Malawi, Mathews Nkhambala has experienced the devastating effects of flooding.

In April 2024, barely a year after Tropical Cyclone Freddy devastated the country's southern region, floods displaced people in Chikwawa district.

Nkhambala fled to higher ground with his wife and four children as floodwaters swept through his village.

"As we reached a safe height, we saw our house swept away right in front of our eyes. Everything I had was gone," he told the BBC.

He lost a harvest of 15 bags of sorghum and part of his farmland. His children were so traumatised that they stopped going to school.

"They refused to go to school for many months. They were so disturbed," he recalled.

After relocating and trying to rebuild his life, Nkhambala is now facing another climate challenge - this time a lack of rain.

"This time we fear there may be no harvest. I have no clue what I will do."

A government assessment after Cyclone Freddy found that Malawi had experienced more than 50 disasters linked to storms, floods, landslides and droughts since 1980, affecting millions of people.

While Uganda and Malawi are suffering the effects of climate change and their governments are asking for assistance adapting to the new global weather patterns, they are among 23 African countries yet to submit National Adaptation Plans (NAPs) to the UN climate convention secretariat.

These are the plans that detail how climate change has affected them and the risks they face, and so help make a case for what assistance they need. Without them, experts say, it becomes difficult to secure funding.

"Our region has experienced cyclical droughts for decades, but there has been no action plan to tackle these climate impacts," said Milton Lorpia, who works for Warrior Squad Foundation in Karamoja region of Uganda.

"If only such a plan were in place and implemented, it would certainly have helped us."

The African Group of Negotiators at the ongoing UN climate summit (COP31) in Turkey is pushing for adaptation finance to be tripled by 2035, from an annual $40bn (£30bn) baseline that it says developed countries committed to providing by 2025. The interpretation of that commitment remains contested.

The proposal was not accepted for formal negotiations at the summit, although African negotiators have continued to push for it.

The funding is intended to help vulnerable countries prepare for and withstand climate change-induced extreme weather, such as droughts, floods and wildfires.

But the European Union, one of the largest providers of climate finance, says the priority should be ensuring existing commitments reach vulnerable countries rather than setting new funding targets.

"We haven't come to the table with additional monies or additional capital. It's about what we have committed already and ensuring it's deployed," Darragh O'Brien, who leads the EU delegation at COP31 on behalf of the Irish presidency of the Council of the EU, told a press conference.

He acknowledged that developing countries faced difficulties accessing available funding, saying the process needed to be improved.

Wopke Hoekstra, the European Commission's climate commissioner, also argued that the summit should focus on delivering existing pledges rather than making new ones.

"If you are a vulnerable nation in the Pacific or one of the LDCs (Least Developed Countries) and the money is in the bank but does not land on the ground then it is effectively meaningless," he said.

'It can kill us': Kenyans fear impact of El Niño with floods predicted

Hoekstra said the EU had provided $30bn of the $100bn in climate finance committed by developed countries in recent years, adding that other wealthy nations should contribute more.

The scale of the need is substantial. According to the UN's Adaptation Gap Report published last year, sub-Saharan Africa requires about $51bn annually in adaptation finance, while the Middle East and North Africa needs $112bn.

Globally, developing countries will need about $300bn annually by 2035, according to the UN's latest report. Yet they received only about 10% of that amount from developed countries in 2024.

Climate-related loss and damage in Africa is projected to cost $440bn between 2020 and 2030, according to Nairobi-based think tank Power Shift Africa.

Under the 2015 Paris climate agreement, developed countries are required to provide financial support to developing nations, including for climate adaptation.

But why have so many African countries failed to prepare plans that could help them identify their needs and build resilience?

"If you look closely, the countries that are yet to submit their NAPs are already dealing with multiple crises, including debt distress, economic pressures and other issues," said David Abudho, climate justice lead at the aid agency, Oxfam.

"Their governments' ability to invest in climate adaptation is limited."

Sheila Apiny, regional climate justice adviser at ActionAid, said the lack of plans reflected a wider shortage of financial and technical support.

"The absence of NAPs in so many countries is, in itself, evidence of an adaptation finance and capacity gap," she argued.

She said this created a vicious cycle - countries lack support to prepare their plans, while not having the plans makes it harder to secure funding for climate resilience.

"When countries lack adequate adaptation planning and, more importantly, the resources to implement those plans, governments are forced into a cycle of responding to disasters instead of preventing or reducing their impacts," said Amos Wemanya, senior climate adviser at Power Shift Africa.

"Instead of investing in early warning systems, climate-resilient agriculture, water security and flood protection, scarce public resources are repeatedly diverted towards emergency relief and reconstruction. This costs more over time and leaves communities increasingly vulnerable."

African negotiators acknowledge that adaptation plans help countries prioritise investments and attract funding, but argue that their absence should not be used to deny them financial support.

"Of course, having a comprehensive NAP helps countries prioritise investments and prepare proposals for climate finance," said Mahlet Eyassu Melkie, a senior strategic adviser to Ethiopia's COP32 presidency.

"But Africa's adaptation financing needs are based on scientific assessments, climate vulnerability, national priorities and regional estimates – not simply on whether every country has submitted a particular planning document."

The UN Development Programme, which has helped more than 45 countries prepare their plans, said NAPs can help governments mobilise international support and coordinate climate action.

Fred Njehu, a Pan-African political strategist at Greenpeace Africa, said their absence could nevertheless create significant obstacles.

"It is fair to acknowledge that missing adaptation plans act as a major functional barrier that severely bottlenecks the speed, volume and quality of international funding a country can access," he said.

But having a plan does not guarantee the money needed to implement it.

"Even countries that have completed their NAPs have not received money anywhere near what they require for implementation of their adaptation plans," Apiny said.

Kenya offers an example of how adaptation measures can help communities cope with climate pressures.

In the country's arid and semi-arid south-east, concrete sand dams slow the flow of seasonal rivers, allowing sand to accumulate and store water underground. Communities can access it during dry periods using hand pumps or by scooping it out.

UK charity Sand Dams Worldwide and its local partner, the Africa Sand Dam Foundation, said they had built about 1,300 such dams, improving access to water as droughts become more frequent and intense.

But many vulnerable communities elsewhere on the continent are still waiting for similar interventions.

Back in drought-hit Karamoja, Lobur wonders how different things might have been if farmers had access to small-scale irrigation schemes.

"We do have some underground water sources in some places. If there were proper plans and programmes, we could have tapped them to grow food, but we are having to live in hunger instead," Lobur said.

"My grandmother keeps reminding us how she lost eight children during a famine-like situation in 1982, and we all fear we might perish like that too."

Survivors of Uganda's deadly landslide seek justice at the UN

items.title: Riccardo Muti: “Music still carries a message of peace”
items.summary: The maestro conducts the Vienna Philharmonic in Rome on Saturday: “You don't need any special preparation to be moved by sacred music”
items.content:
“I believe great music still has the power to convey a message of brotherhood and peace.”

So says Riccardo Muti, the internationally acclaimed Italian conductor, who is arriving in Rome to lead the Vienna Philharmonic on Saturday at the Papal Basilica of St Paul Outside the Walls (Free admission. The concert starts at 9pm).

The programme will feature Mozart's Mass in C major , K. 317, known as the Krönungsmesse ( Coronation Mass ), and his Ave Verum Corpus , as part of the Festival of Sacred Music and Art.

The music will ring out across the Italian capital “at a time when war is gripping countries around the world where, in the past, we managed to reach audiences from Ravenna through the Friendship Concerts, from North Africa to Tehran”.

Joining the Vienna Philharmonic in Rome will be the Siena Cathedral Choir and a quartet of vocal soloists, including Italian singers Rosa Feola and Giovanni Sala.

“You don't need any special preparation, nor do you need to belong to a particular faith, to be moved by the Agnus Dei from the Coronation Mass or the Lacrimosa from Mozart's Requiem . What would be essential, however, is for this music to be heard more often on radio and television and given greater consideration by the media.

"I have nothing against songs,” he continues, “which can have their own depth. But the great European classical tradition – from Monteverdi and Bach to Mozart, Beethoven, Verdi and Brahms – is nourishment for the soul, and it should reach everyone.”

Muti has conducted for Pope Paul VI, Pope John Paul II and later Pope Benedict XVI, “a true musician”. His most recent papal engagement came at Christmas 2025, when he conducted music by Luigi Cherubini for Pope Leo XIV.

It was Herbert von Karajan who first invited Muti to conduct the Vienna Philharmonic. In 1984, Karajan conducted the orchestra in a landmark performance of Mozart's Krönungsmesse at St Peter's Basilica in the Vatican.

“We have just completed our tour of Japan with the Vienna Philharmonic, including a performance at Tokyo's Suntory Hall. The square in front of the concert hall is named after Karajan, who was very fond of the venue.”

Muti recalls that, since 1971, he has missed only one year at the Salzburg Festival, clocking up 55 years of appearances. “But above all, my collaboration with the Vienna Philharmonic has lasted 56 years. Without interruption.”

Over the decades, he has watched the orchestra change. “The first musicians I got to know had lived through the war and played under Furtwängler, Böhm and Toscanini.”

Today, a new generation of musicians is coming through. “Among them are three exceptionally talented Italians whom I will see again in Rome: a principal bassoonist, a principal trombonist and one of the viola players.

"The latter comes from Santo Spirito. When I was young, I used to travel by bus to the conservatoire in Bari, and the route took me through that very village. Given how much I work with young musicians in the Cherubini Orchestra, that connection really struck me.”

The Vienna Philharmonic's greatest asset, Muti believes, remains its distinctive sound, of which he considers himself a guardian.

It is a sound that “you recognise instantly, just as you recognise the voices of Maria Callas or Luciano Pavarotti, but which many people nowadays know only from recordings”.

In the past, however, music directors would devote themselves to a single orchestra, “shaping its sound, as Ormandy did in Philadelphia, and Solti and Barenboim in Chicago, before me.

"Today,” he concludes, “it is fashionable to serve as music director of two orchestras, and perhaps even of an opera house as well. I find that inconceivable.”

items.title: Italy’s Greens at 40: always with a touch of red
items.summary: Founded in 1986, rooted in Alexander Langer’s utopian vision and shaped by anti-nuclear campaigns, Italy’s Greens helped bring environmental issues back to the heart of political debate. Yet they never managed to forge a political identity of their own beyond the left
items.content:
ROME – “We need clean air, even in Parliament,” declared one of the first posters produced by Italy’s Greens. It was 1987, and the Smiling Sun, a symbol borrowed from northern Europe’s anti-nuclear campaigns, was making its debut in Italian national politics. Forty years later, after spells in government and opposition, splits and reunifications, electoral victories and defeats, the Greens are one of Italy’s longest-standing political movements. They have never won a double-digit share of the vote, but have always remained firmly on the left.

The movement was officially founded on 15 and 16 November 1986, when the Federation of Green Lists was established in Finale Ligure. It had already contested some local elections, but it was only a few months after the Chernobyl nuclear disaster that a national political organisation took shape.

It brought together 92 groups, including environmentalists, pacifists, activists from the New Left, Radicals and local campaign organisations. They campaigned against nuclear power, pollution, unchecked urban development and the destruction of the landscape, at a time when the climate crisis had yet to take centre stage in public debate and much of the Italian left remained committed to a traditional model of industrial development.

The project had a strong utopian element. Its first policy convention, held in 1987, was entitled The City of the Sun , a reference to the work of the philosopher Tommaso Campanella and the vision of a peaceful, caring society living in harmony with nature and offering an alternative to traditional structures of power.

The first major victory came that same year. In November 1987, Italians voted in favour of three referendums, promoted by a coalition including the Greens, Radicals and the anti-capitalist left, paving the way for the abandonment of nuclear power.

A few months earlier, in the general election, the Smiling Sun had won 13 seats in the Chamber of Deputies and two in the Senate, bringing organised environmentalism into the Italian Parliament for the first time.

Also in 1987, the Greens joined the governing majority in Palermo’s city council, led by Leoluca Orlando, a leading figure in a period of political renewal and the fight against the Mafia.

The movement’s origins, however, were far from homogeneous. Alongside the Green Lists, the Rainbow Greens emerged in 1989 from an alliance between figures from the Marxist left and the Radical Party, which had spearheaded campaigns for civil rights in Italy.

These represented two distinct political traditions: one saw environmentalism as an opportunity to renew socialism, while the other was rooted in libertarianism and nonviolence.

In the 1989 European elections, the two groups together won more than 6 per cent of the vote. They eventually united in December 1990.

The most significant figure of that period was Alexander Langer, from South Tyrol, a former activist in the extra-parliamentary left-wing group Lotta Continua, a pacifist and a committed European.

For Langer, ecology was not simply an environmental issue but a project to transform society. “Ecological conversion can only succeed if it appears socially desirable,” he wrote in 1994.

He countered the Olympic motto “faster, higher, stronger” with “slower, deeper, gentler”: an invitation to rethink consumption, production and lifestyles.

He died by suicide in 1995, leaving an intellectual legacy that extends far beyond the boundaries of environmental politics.

During the 1990s and 2000s, the Greens became a regular part of centre-left coalitions. Francesco Rutelli, for example, who came from the environmentalist movement, became mayor of Rome in 1993.

The movement helped bring environmental issues into political institutions, but gradually lost electoral support and its capacity to mobilise people.

Its most serious defeat came in 2008, when an electoral alliance with the radical left, known as the Rainbow Left, failed to reach the threshold required to enter Parliament.

That marked the beginning of a 14-years absence from Parliament, while in other European countries, particularly Germany, Green parties were winning double-digit vote shares and assuming government responsibilities.

A new wave of environmental mobilisation emerged with Greta Thunberg and the Fridays for Future movement. In Italy, too, hundreds of thousands of young people took to the streets to demand action against global warming.

Although the movement maintained its independence from political parties, it helped put environmental issues back at the centre of political debate.

In 2022, the Greens, by then renamed Green Europe ( Europa Verde ), returned to Parliament through an alliance with Italian Left ( Sinistra Italiana ), a post-communist left-wing party led by Nicola Fratoianni.

Their joint electoral list, the Greens and Left Alliance ( Alleanza Verdi e Sinistra , or AVS), won more than 6 per cent of the vote in the 2024 European elections.

Today, Green Europe is led by Angelo Bonelli and Fiorella Zabatta, and the Smiling Sun still features in the alliance’s emblem, alongside the red of the left.

Elsewhere in Europe, Green parties have followed different trajectories, becoming major political players in several countries.

In Germany, where the movement, like its Italian counterpart, emerged from the convergence of environmentalism, pacifism and the New Left, the Greens ( Grünen ) entered the federal government for the first time in 1998, with Joschka Fischer serving as foreign minister.

In France, environmentalists have won control of major local administrations, while in Belgium, Austria, Finland and Sweden they have participated in governing coalitions.

The European Green Party was founded in 2004, bringing together the continent’s main environmentalist parties. In Brussels, most sit together in the Greens group, although some belong to the red-green left represented by The Left.

Across Europe, Britain’s Green Party is now on the rise under Zack Polanski, who places strong emphasis not only on environmental issues but also on tackling inequality and expressing solidarity with the Palestinian people.

What has most clearly distinguished Italy’s Greens from their German and northern European counterparts is their difficulty in establishing a political identity independent of the left.

Although they emerged from similar movements, Germany’s Greens have become a party of government capable of appealing to the urban middle classes and forging alliances with conservatives.

That evolution has involved profound ideological shifts, particularly over pacifism: from supporting military intervention in Kosovo in 1999 to backing Ukraine following Russia’s invasion.

In Italy, by contrast, the Greens have remained more closely tied to the traditions of the left, with a more ideologically driven electorate.

There have been contradictions and defeats, particularly in the transition from protest to the responsibilities of government, amid compromises over industrial, energy and military policies.

Yet over four decades, Europe’s Greens have helped transform environmentalism from a minority cause into one of the defining issues of contemporary politics.

The challenge remains the one identified by Langer: to make a different model of society desirable, rather than merely insisting that it is necessary.

items.title: How can we recognise women’s role in architecture? A debate in Sardinia
items.summary: The alliance between feminist struggles and the right to housing is not merely a possibility, but a historical fact. Four days of conversations exploring human geographies at the Pazza Idea festival in Cagliari.
items.content:
From the Mussolini-era assertion that “women have no place in architecture”, a view more or less explicitly echoed by some of the discipline’s most celebrated masters, to the 20th-century rebranding exercises that alternately cast women as the “angel of the house” or the “manager of the mechanised home”, the relationship between women and domestic space has often been framed in adversarial terms by so-called “white” feminist movements.

The emphasis was on emancipation as something that could only be achieved by leaving the dining room behind. But, as Carlotta Cossutta rightly argues, building on the work of Sara Ahmed, precisely at a time when everything teaches us to simplify and to assume that what is easier must necessarily be better, one of the aims of feminist scholarship is to “complicate genealogies”.

There is, in fact, a third way to be found in unexpected places, in hidden voices and those historically silenced. It involves an alliance between feminist struggles and the right to housing, one that moves beyond the binary opposition between oppression and liberation.

This is not merely a viable possibility, but an established historical reality, already rich in experiences that have turned the relationship between domestic and public life into a two-way journey towards women’s self-determination.

Sometimes all it takes is to look beyond the boundaries of the Western middle class, towards those communities that, through a certain degree of racial prejudice, we have regarded as “oppressed”.

Turkish architect Zeynep Çelik, for instance, examining the symbolic and practical significance of the spaces inhabited by Algerian women in the Casbah, showed how rooftop terraces, understood as hybrid spaces between the private and the public, became sites of political resistance to French colonial rule, with women playing a leading role.

Another example is the home as an indispensable space for socialising, solidarity and conspiracy among African Americans. As bell hooks puts it: “In the culture of white supremacy, out in the world, we would not have been able to learn to love and respect ourselves.”

Over recent decades, urban planners, sociologists and researchers in design and architecture working on gender studies have highlighted how, while space undoubtedly shapes gender, it is also within the home that processes through which women become political subjects have acquired public significance.

And yet these are cases, studies and experiences that are rarely taught in schools.

Consequently, the design of our cities, homes and everyday objects remains largely unchanged and is still shaped primarily by those who are least affected by it– because they spend most of their time away from home, do not rely on public services, are shielded from the consequences of poor design or experience little, if any, form of social alienation.

Now that housing has become a central issue on political agendas, feminism needs to reclaim a leading role in shaping a vision of living that is both fulfilling and free. This means rediscovering how domestic knowledge, and the radical epistemology rooted in that experience, have made women experts in their own right and political subjects.

Perhaps it is no coincidence that, while so-called “progressive” institutions periodically and clumsily attempt to absorb the feminist perspective into design, effectively stripping it of its political force, it is the right across the world that seems to have grasped more clearly the subversive potential contained in the old slogan of bread and roses – or, if you prefer, of a room of one’s own and the material means to pay its rent.

And perhaps that is precisely why it continues to mock and oppose it.

Nor is it a coincidence that the public squares where people take to the streets against patriarchal violence, which silences women’s voices and stifles their imagination, are also places where they fight the economic violence of property speculation, which deprives them of the spaces they need to assert their expertise and exercise that capacity to go beyond established boundaries.

To furnish that room, in other words, with the complexity of needs and desires that feminist approaches to living can carry from the dining room into the streets. And back again.

The author will speak at the Pazza Idea Festival, taking place in Cagliari from 19 to 21 November. This year’s edition is entitled “Human Geographies”.

items.title: UK and EU to agree youth mobility scheme, BBC understands
items.summary: The scheme is expected to be approved at Friday's UK-EU summit, with new deals on food trade and carbon emissions also on the table.
items.content:
Up to 100,000 young people from the EU would be allowed to travel, work and study in the UK per year under a new youth mobility scheme set to be agreed on Friday, the BBC understands.

The same number of young Britons would be allowed into Europe under the scheme, expected to be approved at the UK-EU summit in Brussels. Downing Street has not commented on the details, but said talks were "down to the wire" on Thursday.

The prime minister has said a "Channel action plan" on immigration could also be struck, while negotiators are seeking agreements on food trade rules and carbon emissions pricing.

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch has accused Andy Burnham of "reopening the divisions" of the Brexit referendum.

A new youth mobility scheme would aim to make it easier for young people to work and travel both in the EU and UK.

The UK already has schemes in place with 13 non-EU countries including Australia, Canada and India.

In 2024, the EU proposed allowing 18 to 30 year-olds to work or study in the EU and UK for up to four years.

Labour, which was then in opposition, rejected the deal - arguing it amounted to reinstating freedom of movement.

Since coming to government, the party has suggested it would consider a more restricted scheme with a time limit, a cap on the numbers coming to the UK and a ban on participants from claiming benefits.

The UK's request to limit numbers has proved to be a sticking point in negotiation ahead of the summit, along with the EU's request that EU students should pay the same tuition fees at UK universities as domestic students.

Speaking to broadcasters on Thursday evening, Burnham was asked if there were any circumstances in which the UK would walk away from a deal on Friday.

"There would always be those circumstances because I'm in this to get the best deal for Britain, always," he said.

"But what's in it for us is the possibility of lower food prices and I can't turn my back on that, lower costs for business, cutting red tape, and a really big win potentially of more collaboration on immigration - a Channel action plan - which is a really big deal if we can land that tomorrow.

"So I hope people can understand why I have pushed this because it could be a really good deal for Britain."

Burnham previously said the UK and EU could link up their law enforcement efforts, including sharing more data and criminal records of foreign nationals.

The prime minister's spokesman has said if a deal were secured, the government would introduce legislation to Parliament next week to implement changes.

The Brexit debate is back – and there are nerves about what happens next

Faisal Islam: What's in the Brexit reset food deal and are there trade-offs?

The EU that Burnham is eyeing up is very different to the one Britain left

An agreement on trade could remove checks and paperwork faced by food companies exporting to the EU.

The government argues this could add £5bn to the economy and cut food prices.

However, it could mean the UK will have to follow certain EU rules on products, for example on gene-edited crops or labelling.

Burnham has also said the summit would allow the UK to raise concerns about the Made in Europe scheme, which is designed to protect industries from unfair Chinese competition.

Burnham has previously suggested he could commit Labour to building a closer long-term future relationship with Europe, including asking to rejoin the organisation as a full member - however, he has ruled out major changes before the next election.

The party's 2024 manifesto promised not to return to the EU, the single market, customs union or freedom of movement, which allows EU citizens to live and work elsewhere in the bloc without a visa.

Earlier this week, former deputy prime minister David Lammy urged the prime minister to go into the next general election promising to rejoin the EU.

However, the subject has divided his cabinet with one minister warning of the costs that would come with reversing Brexit.

Reform UK leader Nigel Farage, speaking to The Sun , external , said he does "not believe for a minute" the country would "ever vote to rejoin" the EU.

He added: "I think what Burnham is doing is playing a very cynical political game. He's trying to pick up votes from the Lib Dems, pick up votes from the Greens, and using it as a massive distraction from all the problems that he can't deal with."

Speaking to the BBC's Today programme on Thursday, Badenoch said she wanted to see easier trading with the EU, but "not trade at any cost".

She also said the new deals could see UK companies having to follow EU rules, even those that do not trade with the bloc.

Liberal Democrat leader Sir Ed Davey told BBC Newsnight that while he agreed with Burnham on "the harms of Brexit", he did not think the prime minister was "going to go anywhere near far enough".

"We need to go further and faster," he said, including returning to freedom of movement - which Sir Ed said would help tackle immigration and boost the UK economy.

items.title: China issues Mount Fuji warning as family of missing climber offers reward
items.summary: The $75,000 reward offered by Chen Jie's family has sparked fears of more reckless climbing attempts.
items.content:
The Chinese embassy in Japan has warned its citizens against off-season ascents of Mount Fuji amid concerns that the hefty reward offered by a missing hiker's family could encourage more reckless climbing.

Chen Jie, 25, vanished on 8 November on the mountain. His family is offering 500,000 yuan ($75,000; £57,300) to anyone who finds him alive, and 100,000 yuan to anyone who recovers his body, say Chinese and Japanese media reports.

Strong winds and blizzards pose serious risks during the closed season, especially as shelter and first-aid centres are not operational, the embassy said on Tuesday.

Mount Fuji's official climbing season runs from around early July to early September.

Earlier this year, authorities of Yamanashi province, where the northern part of Mount Fuji sits, had said that people who attempt to climb Mount Fuji during off-peak seasons and then require rescue by helicopter will have to pay for the service from next year on.

Authorities will also require those looking to scale Fuji during the off-season to submit detailed climbing plans.

"We hope that these measures will cause people to rethink what climbing Mount Fuji during the winter is like," Kotaro Nagasaki, the prefecture governor, said at the time.

On Wednesday, Nagasaki told reporters that attempts to find the missing climber could lead to "secondary disasters"

According to Japanese news outlet the Mainichi Shimbun, Nagasaki appeared to appeal to Chen's family, saying: "I understand that your family is important, but please refrain from doing anything that could endanger others."

Some social media users in Japan have similarly expressed fears would entice people to venture into the mountains ill-prepared and lead to more accidents,

Yamanashi police said Chen had set out on his hike on 8 November with two friends, who turned back after they realised the mountain was closed and that they weren't suitably equipped for the conditions of the trails.

Chen pressed on alone from the fifth station of the Yoshida Trail, which sits at around 2,300m (7545ft) above sea level.

A friend last heard from Chen at 10:30 that day, when he sent a video message saying: "I'm going up the mountain... There's no one in sight."

The highest point of Mount Fuji, which is Japan's tallest peak, stands at 3,776m.

Local authorities launched a search for Chen on 10 November, but it had to be halted several times because of poor weather.

Chen's father reportedly arrived in Japan on 13 November. It is not clear when he posted the reward offer.

Lost on Mount Fuji off-season? You'll have to pay for your rescue

items.title: FFmpeg 9.1 'Gauss'
items.summary: Article URL: https://ffmpeg.org/download.html#release_9.1 Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50569998 Points: 43 # Comments: 9
items.content:
FFmpeg only provides source code. Below are some links that provide it already compiled and ready to go.

You can retrieve the source code through Git by using the command:

FFmpeg has always been a very experimental and developer-driven project. It is a key component in many multimedia projects and has new features added constantly. Development branch snapshots work really well 99% of the time so people are not afraid to use them.

Since FFmpeg is developed with Git , multiple repositories from developers and groups of developers are available.

All FFmpeg releases are cryptographically signed with our public PGP key and should be verified for authenticity.

To verify a release: Import our public key into your local keyring: $ curl https://ffmpeg.org/ffmpeg-devel.asc | gpg --import Download a release tarball and its corresponding signature. Verify the signature: $ gpg --verify ffmpeg-4.3.2.tar.xz.asc ffmpeg-4.3.2.tar.xz gpg: Signature made Sun 21 Feb 2021 06:35:15 AEST gpg: using RSA key FCF986EA15E6E293A5644F10B4322F04D67658D8 gpg: issuer "ffmpeg-devel@ffmpeg.org" gpg: Good signature from "FFmpeg release signing key " [full] Optionally, you can verify that git and tarball match, the only differences should be the absence of .git* files in the tarball and a VERSION file in the tarball containing the version. The git tags should be signed with EDDSA key DD1EC9E8DE085C629B3E1846B18E8928B3948D64

A release that also has a .pq.asc file carries post-quantum signatures ( RFC 9980 ) made with both of these keys:

GnuPG cannot verify these yet; use sq 1.4 or later built with a cryptographic backend that supports these algorithms (OpenSSL 3.5 or RustCrypto), both of these must succeed: $ sq verify --signature-file ffmpeg-9.0.2.tar.xz.pq.asc --signer-file ffmpeg-mldsa87-ed448.cert.pgp ffmpeg-9.0.2.tar.xz $ sq verify --signature-file ffmpeg-9.0.2.tar.xz.pq.asc --signer-file ffmpeg-slhdsa256s.cert.pgp ffmpeg-9.0.2.tar.xz

Approximately every 6 months the FFmpeg project makes a new major release. Between major releases point releases will appear that add important bug fixes but no new features. Note that these releases are intended for distributors and system integrators. Users that wish to compile from source themselves are strongly encouraged to consider using the development branch (see above), this is the only version on which FFmpeg developers actively work. The release branches only cherry pick selected changes from the development branch, which therefore receives much more and much faster bug fixes such as additional features and security patches.

9.1 was released on 2026-11-20. It is the latest stable FFmpeg release from the 9.1 release branch, which was cut from master on 2026-10-24.

9.0.2 was released on 2026-09-18. It is the latest stable FFmpeg release from the 9.0 release branch, which was cut from master on 2026-06-26.

8.1.3 was released on 2026-09-21. It is the latest stable FFmpeg release from the 8.1 release branch, which was cut from master on 2026-03-08.

8.0.3 was released on 2026-06-18. It is the latest stable FFmpeg release from the 8.0 release branch, which was cut from master on 2025-08-09.

7.1.5 was released on 2026-06-20. It is the latest stable FFmpeg release from the 7.1 release branch, which was cut from master on 2024-09-24.

6.1.6 was released on 2026-06-20. It is the latest stable FFmpeg release from the 6.1 release branch, which was cut from master on 2023-10-29.

5.1.10 was released on 2026-06-21. It is the latest stable FFmpeg release from the 5.1 release branch, which was cut from master on 2022-07-13.

4.4.8 was released on 2026-06-21. It is the latest stable FFmpeg release from the 4.4 release branch, which was cut from master on 2021-04-08.

Older versions are available at the Old Releases page. Releases are usually moved there after the last downstream drops support.

items.title: GIMP now has UI tests
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.gimp.org/news/2026/11/16/gimp-ui-tests/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50569985 Points: 74 # Comments: 74
items.content:
GIMP has a lot of intertwined menus, dialogs and tools. When we change a part of the interface, another may stop working and sometimes, the problem can be missed until a user reports it.

To find these problems early, a new GUI testing platform was implemented. A typical GUI test starts GIMP , clicks menus and buttons, and then checks the result. These tests run automatically each time we merge contributor changes.

GIMP already has unit tests. A unit test checks one small part of the code, for example how GIMP reads an XCF file. But our unit tests were not opening a real window. So it coult not tell us if a dialog opens, or if a menu item did its job.

Note that GIMP already had tests of GUI code, usually interacting directly with the core code, and sometimes even simulating input devices’ events (pointer movements, clicks, drags…). But nothing can beat interacting with the real interface. Furthermore such legacy tests directly hijacking core code come with their own problems, such as breaking all too often (and not because they detected a bug), all while not being able to detect whole categories of bugs.

UI tests check the program as a whole, in the same way as you use it.

Each test starts a real GIMP and does one small task. Then it reads the result from GIMP . If the result is not correct, the test fails and tells us what went wrong.

The tests do not need a screen. Each test starts a small, hidden desktop, runs GIMP in it, and removes it at the end. Because of this, the tests can run on our CI servers, where no screen is available.

To find a button or a menu, the tests do not look at the pixels on the screen. They use the accessibility information that GIMP gives to tools such as screen readers. This has one more good result: when we make GIMP easier to test, we also make it easier to use with a screen reader, hence improve the software accessibility.

The tests use dogtail , a Python tool for UI tests. To run GIMP on a server with no screen, dogtail needed a new feature. We contributed this feature upstream, to dogtail itself, so other projects can use it too.

At this time, the tests run only on Linux (both X11 and Wayland) since dogtail does not support Windows or macOs.

Adding even these few simple tests considerably increases confidence that the GIMP build has worked, and also shows the test infrastructure is working and useful.

13 tests is a good start, but GIMP has many more dialogs and tools. If you want to help, you can write a test for the part of GIMP that you use the most.

We wrote a guide that shows how to write a new test and how to find the cause when a test fails: UI tests on developer.gimp.org .

We hope this work will help us find bugs earlier and keep GIMP working well for everyone.
