items.title: PostgreSQL 19
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/19.0/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50569890 Points: 75 # Comments: 2
items.content:
PostgreSQL 19 contains many new features and enhancements, including:

New REPACK command that reclaims disk space and reorganizes table contents, which can improve query performance. REPACK (CONCURRENTLY) allows repacking without blocking reads and writes to the table.

pg_plan_advice extension for controlling query planner decisions and pg_stash_advice extension that applies plan advice automatically based on the query.

Better performance in many areas, including automatic scaling of the number of I/O worker processes, quicker foreign-key checks, and further planning and execution optimizations.

Logical replication can now be enabled without a server restart when wal_level is set to replica .

Support for “ read-your-writes ” consistency on standbys via the new WAIT command.

Parallel autovacuum of table indexes and autovacuum prioritization through a new scoring system.

The above items and other new features of PostgreSQL 19 are explained in more detail in the sections below.

A dump/restore using pg_dumpall or use of pg_upgrade or logical replication is required for those wishing to migrate data from any previous release. See Section 18.6 for general information on migrating to new major releases.

Version 19 contains a number of changes that may affect compatibility with previous releases. Observe the following incompatibilities:

Add server variable password_expiration_warning_threshold to warn about password expiration (Gilles Darold, Nathan Bossart) §

Issue a warning after successful MD5 password authentication (Nathan Bossart) §

The warning can be disabled via server variable md5_password_warnings . MD5 passwords were marked as deprecated in PostgreSQL 18.

PostgreSQL only supported RADIUS over UDP , which is unfixably insecure.

Force standard_conforming_strings to always be on in the database server (Tom Lane) §

Dumps created using pre- PostgreSQL 19 versions of pg_dump or pg_dumpall , and using standard_conforming_strings = off , will not properly load into PostgreSQL 19 and later servers. Users should create dumps using PostgreSQL 19 or later versions of these applications, or use standard_conforming_strings = on .

Client applications still support operations with servers having standard_conforming_strings = off , for compatibility with old servers. The server variable escape_string_warning has been removed as unnecessary.

Disallow carriage returns and line feeds in database, role, and tablespace names (Mahendra Singh Thalor) §

pg_upgrade will also disallow upgrading of clusters that use such names. This was changed to avoid security problems.

Change the default index opclasses for inet and cidr data types from btree_gist to GiST (Tom Lane) § §

The btree_gist inet / cidr opclasses are broken because they can exclude rows that should be returned. pg_upgrade will disallow upgrading of clusters with btree_gist inet / cidr indexes.

Disallow system columns from being used in COPY FROM ... WHERE (Tom Lane) §

Change a json_array() call which returns no rows to return an empty JSON array (Richard Guo) §

Cause transactions to pass their READ ONLY and DEFERRABLE status to postgres_fdw sessions (Etsuro Fujita) §

This means READ ONLY transactions can no longer modify rows processed by postgres_fdw sessions.

Change default of max_locks_per_transaction from 64 to 128 (Heikki Linnakangas) §

Lock size allocation has changed, so effectively settings must now be doubled to match their capacity in previous releases.

This has been replaced by four new variables; see Section E.1.3.1.2 .

Previously JIT was enabled by default, and activated based on optimizer costs, but this costing has been determined to be unreliable. This change requires sites that are doing many large analytical queries to manually enable JIT .

Change parallel vacuum leaders and workers to share the cost-based vacuum delay limit (Bharath Rupireddy) §

Previously each worker process slept based only on the cost it incurred itself, so a parallel vacuum could consume several times the budget set by vacuum_cost_limit . With this change, VACUUM with parallel workers and cost-based delay enabled might run slower than in previous releases.

Rename column sync_error_count to sync_table_error_count in system view pg_stat_subscription_stats (Vignesh C) §

This is necessary since sequence errors are now tracked separately.

Rename wait event type BUFFERPIN to BUFFER and rename wait event BufferPin to BufferCleanup (Andres Freund) §

Remove wait event BufferContent and add more precise wait events BufferShared , BufferShareExclusive , and BufferExclusive (Andres Freund) §

Change index access method handlers to use a static IndexAmRoutines structure, rather than dynamically allocated ones (Matthias van de Meent) §

Remove optimizer hook get_relation_info_hook and add better-placed hook build_simple_rel_hook (Robert Haas) §

Change psql 's \crosstabview command to honor the \pset null setting (Chao Li) §

Change full text search and pg_trgm to use the database's locale provider for character classification when parsing text (Jeff Davis) §

Previously, characters were classified using libc, regardless of the locale provider. In databases with a locale provider other than libc (e.g., ICU , builtin ) and where the locale configured through that locale provider behaves differently from the LC_CTYPE setting configured for the database, particularly a LC_CTYPE of C , the output of some full text search and pg_trgm functions could change. When upgrading such databases using pg_upgrade , it is recommended to reindex all indexes which use full text search and pg_trgm after the upgrade, and to recompute any stored tsvector values.

Change how fuzzystrmatch functions handle non- ASCII characters (Peter Eisentraut, Jeff Davis) § §

dmetaphone() and dmetaphone_alt() now upper-case their input using the database's default collation rather than always using libc, and soundex() , metaphone() , and difference() now treat only ASCII letters as letters. When upgrading with pg_upgrade , it is recommended to reindex any indexes that use these functions after the upgrade.

This encoding was complex and rarely used. Databases using it will need to be dumped and restored with a different encoding.

Below you will find a detailed account of the changes between PostgreSQL 19 and the previous major release.

Allow NOT IN clauses to be converted to more efficient ANTI JOIN s when NULLs are not present (Richard Guo) §

Allow more LEFT JOIN s to be converted to ANTI JOIN s (Tender Wang, Richard Guo) §

Allow use of Memoize for ANTI JOIN s with unique inner sides (Richard Guo) §

Allow some aggregate processing to be performed before joins (Richard Guo, Antonin Houska) § § §

Improve hash join's handling of tuples with NULL join keys (Tom Lane) §

Allow Append and MergeAppend to consider explicit incremental sorts (Richard Guo) §

Convert IS [NOT] DISTINCT FROM NULL to IS [NOT] NULL during constant folding (Richard Guo) §

Simplify IS [NOT] DISTINCT FROM to equality/inequality operators when inputs are proven non-nullable (Richard Guo) §

Perform earlier constant folding of var IS [NOT] NULL in the optimizer (Richard Guo) §

Simplify COALESCE() and ROW(...) IS [NOT] NULL to avoid evaluating unnecessary arguments (Richard Guo) § §

Simplify IS [NOT] TRUE/FALSE/UNKNOWN to plain boolean expressions when the input is proven non-nullable (Richard Guo) §

Speed up join selectivity computations for large optimizer statistics targets (Ilia Evdokimov, David Geier) §

Add proper optimizer statistics for functions returning boolean values (Tom Lane) §

Allow extended statistics on virtual generated columns (Yugo Nagata) §

Allow function pg_restore_extended_stats() to restore optimizer extended statistics (Corey Huinker, Michael Paquier, Chao Li) § § § §

Add function pg_clear_extended_stats() to remove extended statistics (Corey Huinker, Michael Paquier) §

Adjust the optimizer to consider startup costs of partial paths (Robert Haas, Tomas Vondra) §

Allow negative values of pg_aggregate . aggtransspace to indicate unbounded memory usage (Richard Guo) §

This information is used by the optimizer in planning memory usage.

Improve performance of foreign key constraint checks (Junwang Zhao, Amit Langote, Chao Li) § §

Improve asynchronous I/O read-ahead scheduling for large requests (Andres Freund) § § §

Allow io_method method worker to automatically control needed background workers (Thomas Munro) §

The new server variables are io_min_workers , io_max_workers , io_worker_idle_timeout , and io_worker_launch_interval .

Allow query table scans to mark pages as all-visible in the visibility map (Melanie Plageman) §

Allow autovacuum to use parallel autovacuum workers (Daniil Davydov) § §

The maximum number of workers is controlled by server variable autovacuum_max_parallel_workers and per-table storage parameter autovacuum_parallel_workers .

Allow TID Range Scans to be parallelized (Cary Huang, David Rowley) §

Improve COPY FROM performance for text and CSV input using SIMD CPU instructions (Nazir Bilal Yavuz, Shinya Kato) §

Improve NOTIFY to only wake up backends that are listening to specified notifications (Joel Jacobson) §

items.title: OpenSSL: Buffer overflow in EVP_EncodeBlock() (CVE-2026-121481, CVSS 9.8)
items.summary: Article URL: https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/33652 Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50569226 Points: 143 # Comments: 77
items.content:
This fixes "Buffer overflow in EVP_EncodeBlock()" ( CVE-2026-121481 ) by returning -1 for invalid inputs to EVP_EncodeBlock() : NULL input or output buffers, negative lengths, and lengths for which the encoded size does not fit in an int . The OpenSSL SRT has asked for it to be fixed publicly; the advisory is still pending.

Returning -1 for invalid inputs is the most straightforward fix, and matches what happens in wolfSSL's compatibility layer for OpenSSL's EVP_EncodeBlock() .

I'm suggesting a similar guard for EVP_DecodeBlock() . No length limit is needed here because the decoded length always fits in an int , but it is a good idea to reject NULL buffers and negative lengths.

Moreover, I propose to fix the incorrect length check in the base64encode() function of http_client.c , which rejected only len > INT_MAX .

I am adding tests in test/base64_dec_avx2_test.c to cover the new behavior, and documenting the -1 returns in doc/man3/EVP_EncodeInit.pod .

Exploiting this vulnerability from the command line is possible by passing a large -proxy_pass to openssl s_client . I confirmed that GOST accepts these large passwords out of the box. However, the password has to be supplied through an environment variable ( env:VAR ), otherwise the command line will be too long.

Note: the pattern of CVE-2026-121481 is similar to that of CVE-2021-23840 .

The reason will be displayed to describe this comment to others. Learn more .

This patch changes functions so they can fail. Can you please also ensure the call sites check the return value of this function?

This patch changes functions so they can fail. Can you please also ensure the call sites check the return value of this function?

Unless these callers can plausibly trigger the error conditions, I am not sure it needs to be done as part of this PR.

The reason will be displayed to describe this comment to others. Learn more .

I am really worried about the negative return value being added. Existing third party callers might not be ready to handle this correctly (i.e. if they cast the return to size_t without checking). Could we instead return 0? (In all the added error returns in this PR.)

The reason will be displayed to describe this comment to others. Learn more .

I'm okay making any changes that you suggest, but are you really sure about this?

Both EVP_EncodeBlock() and EVP_DecodeBlock() can legitimately return 0, so 0 is not an error for either function. EVP_EncodeBlock() returns 0 when dlen == 0, and EVP_DecodeBlock() returns 0 when the input is empty after trimming.

Also, for EVP_DecodeBlock(), the current failure paths (e.g., trimmed length not a multiple of invalid base64 characters) all return -1. So, I wanted to make sure that both EVP_EncodeBlock() and EVP_DecodeBlock() consistently return -1 on any error. As I mentioned before, returning -1 is also what WolfSSL does in its OpenSSL compatibility layer.

I understand the concern that third-party callers may cast the return to size_t without checking. But are we not making things more difficult for third-party calls if both 0 and -1 can indicate errors, or if the existing EVP_DecodeBlock() errors will be changed from -1 to 0?

PS: I'm happy to make a separate commit for the problematic call site checks that Norbert pointed out.

The reason will be displayed to describe this comment to others. Learn more .

maybe return 0 instead? Since EVP_EncodeBlock is defined in the docs as returning the number of bytes encoded, a 0 return would be reasonable, as it accurately indicates no bytes were encoded. We could additionally add an ERR_raise_data to indicate the reason why it happened.

The reason will be displayed to describe this comment to others. Learn more .

I've already been tagged for trying to raise an error on a success case - and probably legitimately - 0 is a success case.

The reason will be displayed to describe this comment to others. Learn more .

So I think this is the incorrect fix, We already for STYLE.md say we should NOT add special case errors like this where we get a failure case that looks like a success. We should document that this function does not accept negative lengths, and simply use OPENSSL_ASSERT here.

Making something return a magic value that appears to be a success for this just adds dead code and impossible to reach and untested error cases everywhere.

The reason will be displayed to describe this comment to others. Learn more .

this PR also adds cases not in the report, and the report's reproducer is completely synthetic, and probably should not be a CVE without evidence it really happens. I suggest this should be fixed in documentation

The reason will be displayed to describe this comment to others. Learn more .

The reason will be displayed to describe this comment to others. Learn more .

Thanks for all the feedback! Following this discussion, I'm suggesting OPENSSL_assert() here.

The reason will be displayed to describe this comment to others. Learn more .

This also rejects an empty input passed as f == NULL with dlen == 0. That call used to work: it wrote the NUL terminator and returned 0. An application encoding an empty buffer it never allocated would now get -1. Could you reject f == NULL only when dlen > 0? EVP_DecodeBlock() has the same issue, and there t is not written either when n == 0.

The reason will be displayed to describe this comment to others. Learn more .

Thanks for pointing this out! I've fixed the PR to preserve all existing well-defined behavior.

Small note here: for this input, the AVX2 path has src + 0, which is undefined behavior if src is NULL. So, I'm suggesting a code change that handles this case before invoking the AVX2 path.

items.title: Vint Cerf on why TCP/IP was never patented
items.summary: Article URL: https://seremot.com/p/vint-cerf-on-why-tcpip-was-never Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50568861 Points: 79 # Comments: 24
items.content:
EXTRA, extra! Today I’m launching Future Stories, my own podcast about technology, science and the way we live.

The first guest is Vint Cerf . He co-designed TCP/IP with Bob Kahn in the 1970s, the rules that let the world’s networks talk to each other. Interviewing him was on my bucket list for years. When I was at Cloudflare I thought about asking him many times, but I was a bit shy. He’s Vint Cerf, after all. This year I finally asked, and he said yes.

We talked over Zoom (not using Zoom again) on October 14. He’s 83, he left Google this year after more than twenty years, and he’s helping start a company, Tolero, that is building software for an Internet between planets. His words: “the speed of light is too slow.”

“Who will our allies be 25 years from now? And we didn’t know. So we thought the only way we can be assured that the allies will have access to this is to simply open it up.”

First, a bug related one (ring a bell? those never stopped over the years…) . Vint once spent two weeks on a program that failed at random, so he couldn’t reproduce it. He finally asked his best friend, Steve Crocker, to step through it with him. At one point Crocker said “that’s the problem”, and he was right. Thirty seconds, after two weeks. Vint’s takeaway is that this is why collaboration matters.

Then a bottle of glitter . In late 1989 three commercial Internet services started in the United States, and one of them was called CERFnet , in San Diego. They first wanted to call it SURFnet , because surfing the Internet, but a network in the Netherlands had a name too close to it. So they asked Vint if they could use his.

He had a moment of “what if they screw it up?” , then decided that people name kids after other people and nobody blames the person they were named after. At the launch, he and the network’s director smashed a plastic bottle of glitter over a Cisco router.

He also tried to connect Minitel , the French online service, to MCI Mail, the email service he built in the 1980s. MCI Mail was designed to link to everything. It reached the telegraph system, which he calls 19th-century stuff, and fax. It even reached the post office: type a postal address into the email and they printed it, put it in an envelope and mailed it. Minitel refused to connect, and he says he still doesn’t understand why.

One more, from outside the interview: In 2020, someone on the Internet-history mailing list (I’m on it) asked if anyone had ever seen Vint without a three-piece suit. One reply: “I have seen Vint in a t-shirt!” Vint answered with just a photo, “IP on Everything”, from a 1992 engineers’ meeting where, in his words, he “felt compelled” to do an “IP on Everything” striptease. The thread is public .

We didn’t go very deep into AI. Time was short, and it’s not his main field these days. But even there, he has a clear way of thinking about it. And near the end he shows a piece of the original ARPANET on camera, and talks about his worry that the next century won’t be able to read what we leave behind.

“I’m worried that the 22nd century won’t know what happened in the 21st because all of our records will have evaporated or will be uninterpretable.”

You can also read the transcript at ourfuturestories.eu/vint-cerf , or listen in your favourite podcast app: ourfuturestories.eu/subscribe . A Portuguese article about it is on SAPO . Short clips are coming in the next days.

This is a passion project. The idea is to tell good stories, the kind that hold up over time. If you like it, subscribe, share it with a friend, and tell me who I should talk to next, you can do it here: ourfuturestories.eu/#contact .

Fun fact: in 2024 I did a segment on the 50 years of the TCP paper on my previous podcast, This Week in NET at Cloudflare. My guests were three then-colleagues: Mark Nottingham (standards), Marwan Fayed (research) and Lucas Pardue (web protocols, co-chair of the IETF’s QUIC working group). You can listen here (or below).

The paper is “A Protocol for Packet Network Intercommunication”, by Vint Cerf and Bob Kahn, published in May 1974 in IEEE Transactions on Communications. It described TCP, a way to join many packet networks into a network of networks. TCP was later split into TCP and IP, and in 1983 they became the core of the Internet that DARPA launched.

items.title: Black Friday Laifen: offerte imperdibili su asciugacapelli, spazzolini e rasoi. Neo e Mini protagonisti
items.summary: Dal 19 al 30 novembre Laifen sconta alcuni dei suoi prodotti più richiesti: il Neo e il Mini scendono di prezzo, insieme allo spazzolino Wave Pro e ai rasoi P3. Ecco tutte le offerte e quanto si risparmia ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Dagli asciugacapelli ad alta velocità agli spazzolini elettrici, fino ai rasoi, Laifen propone in offerta dispositivi pensati per semplificare i gesti quotidiani pensati per la cura della persona.

In occasione del Black Friday e del Cyber Monday, dal 19 al 30 novembre 2026 sul sito ufficiale Laifen si potranno acquistare a prezzo scontato diversi prodotti della gamma, con Neo e Mini tra i protagonisti delle offerte, insieme allo spazzolino Wave Pro e ai rasoi della serie P3.

Laifen Neo è pensato per chi vuole ridurre i tempi di asciugatura senza rinunciare al controllo della temperatura, anche quando si utilizza il phon frequentemente.

Al suo interno troviamo un motore digitale V-Max di nuova generazione, dotato di 13 pale in lega di alluminio aeronautico, che genera un flusso d'aria potente e uniforme con una potenza nominale di 1.500 W.

La temperatura viene monitorata costantemente da un sistema intelligente che contribuisce a limitare l'esposizione dei capelli a temperature eccessive, mentre gli ioni negativi aiutano a contrastare l'elettricità statica e a ridurre l'effetto crespo.

La struttura leggera, con un peso di appena 390 grammi, lo rende facile da maneggiare anche durante l'utilizzo prolungato. Il sistema LED a tre colori permette inoltre di riconoscere a colpo d'occhio la temperatura selezionata.

Neo dispone anche di una modalità dedicata ai bambini, che riduce la temperatura e la potenza del flusso d'aria per rendere l'asciugatura più delicata sui capelli e sul cuoio capelluto sensibile.

Rispetto ai 149,99 euro di listino, Laifen Neo è ora in promozione a 113,99 euro nella versione con tre ugelli magnetici intercambiabili : quello standard per l'asciugatura quotidiana, il concentratore per dirigere il flusso d'aria per realizzare la piega e il diffusore per distribuire l'aria in modo più uniforme, valorizzando il movimento naturale dei capelli.

La promozione coinvolge anche il modello Neo Special, proposto a 135,99 euro anziché 169,99 euro.

Rispetto al Neo, Laifen Neo Special aggiunge la Nourishing Mode a 58 °C, che permette di nebulizzare il proprio olio per capelli attraverso un beccuccio dedicato e le apposite Nourishing Pod ricaricabili, distribuendo il trattamento in modo uniforme su lunghezze e punte.

Il motore brushless da 110.000 giri al minuto genera un flusso d'aria fino a 22 m/s, mentre il controllo termico monitora la temperatura 100 volte al secondo.

Nella promozione rientra anche Laifen Air , il modello più essenziale e leggero della gamma, disponibile a 54,99 euro.

Chi cerca un asciugacapelli meno ingombrante può guardare a Laifen Mini: rispetto al modello SE, il volume è stato ridotto del 33%, mentre il peso si ferma a 299 grammi.

Anche l'impugnatura è stata ridisegnata, con uno spessore inferiore di 5 mm per migliorare la presa e rendere più comodo l'utilizzo. Nonostante le dimensioni contenute, Mini mantiene la tecnologia di asciugatura ad alta velocità e una potenza di 1.100 W.

Come il Neo, integra una modalità dedicata ai bambini, che riduce la temperatura del flusso d'aria per un'asciugatura più delicata.

La confezione comprende un beccuccio magnetico per lo styling e una custodia da viaggio, mentre in occasione del Black Friday è incluso anche un supporto magnetico da parete in omaggio.

Laifen propone sconti anche nel comparto oral care con Wave Pro , uno spazzolino elettrico che unisce movimenti oscillanti a 60° e 66.000 vibrazioni al minuto, seguendo i principi della tecnica di spazzolamento Modified Bass.

Questa combinazione è pensata per raggiungere con precisione le diverse zone della bocca e rendere più efficace la pulizia quotidiana.

Durante l'utilizzo, un sensore intelligente rileva la pressione esercitata sui denti e interviene regolando la velocità del motore quando viene applicata una forza eccessiva.

Attraverso l'app Laifen è possibile personalizzare lo spazzolamento, scegliendo intensità, ampiezza e velocità dei movimenti, oltre a consultare i report delle singole sessioni. Sono disponibili due modalità, per la pulizia quotidiana e quella profonda, mentre la batteria offre un'autonomia dichiarata fino a 70 giorni.

Wave Pro supporta inoltre la ricarica wireless ed è impermeabile con certificazione IPX8.

Per la rasatura c'è Laifen P3 Pro, un rasoio elettrico caratterizzato da una struttura in alluminio lavorato CNC e da una finestra trasparente che permette di vedere il motore interno.

Il sistema di rasatura utilizza tre testine e due motori lineari ad alta velocità, che lavorano insieme per accompagnare i movimenti sul viso e seguire i diversi contorni. Può essere utilizzato sia a secco sia sulla pelle bagnata ed è dotato di certificazione IPX7, che ne consente il risciacquo con acqua.

La batteria offre un'autonomia dichiarata fino a 100 minuti e si ricarica tramite USB-C. È presente anche una modalità viaggio, pensata per evitare accensioni accidentali quando il rasoio viene riposto in borsa o in valigia.

In occasione del Black Friday Laifen P3 Pro scende a 149,99 euro, rispetto ai 199,99 euro di listino. Anche il modello P3 è in promozione a 129,99 euro , anziché 169,99 euro.

items.title: Samsung Secrets: con Vision AI Companion lo Smart TV ha sempre la risposta pronta a ogni tua richiesta
items.summary: Samsung Vision AI Companion trasforma il tuo Smart TV in un vero assistente AI: capisce cosa ti piace, risponde alle curiosità su ciò che guardi e trova il film giusto al posto tuo. Ecco come funziona ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Quando ti siedi sul divano a fine giornata con l'idea di rilassarti davanti a un buon film, c'è un rituale che si ripete quasi sempre: passare venti minuti a saltare da un'app all'altra, digitare titoli lettera per lettera con le frecce del telecomando o prendere in mano lo smartphone per cercare chi è quell'attore che hai già visto da qualche parte. Eppure, se in salotto hai un televisore Samsung AI TV, esiste un modo molto più rapido e coinvolgente per trovare subito il film o l’informazione che stai cercando.

Si chiama Samsung Vision AI Companion ed è uno degli elementi più evoluti dell'ecosistema Tizen OS dei Samsung AI TV . Non è il solito assistente vocale a cui devi impartire comandi rigidi sperando che capisca il titolo esatto: è un ambiente conversazionale progettato espressamente per il grande schermo, che capisce il contesto, ricorda cosa ti piace e soprattutto ti risponde in linguaggio naturale, fornendoti risposte su ciò che stai guardando o stai cercando.

Il limite più grande della ricerca vocale tradizionale sui televisori è sempre stato lo stesso: o sai esattamente cosa cercare, oppure finisci davanti a una lista di risultati generici. Vision AI Companion ribalta questo approccio sfruttando la comprensione del linguaggio naturale e modelli linguistici avanzati come Google Gemini, integrando inoltre l'accesso a strumenti come Perplexity direttamente dal TV.

In pratica, puoi parlare al televisore esattamente come faresti con un amico che conosce a memoria tutti i cataloghi streaming . Puoi chiedergli: “t rovami un film di fantascienza ambientato nello spazio che sia molto realistico ", oppure “ consigliami un thriller psicologico uscito negli ultimi anni con colpi di scena” . La parte più comoda arriva subito dopo la risposta: Vision AI Companion non si limita a elencarti dei nomi su schermo, ma ti indica immediatamente su quale piattaforma di streaming installata sul TV puoi vederli, con il collegamento diretto per far partire la riproduzione con un solo clic.

A differenza degli assistenti tradizionali, dove ogni comando riparte da zero, Vision AI Companion tiene traccia della conversazione. Se durante la serata gli chiedi qualche titolo simile a un film che hai appena apprezzato e, dopo qualche minuto, gli domandi semplicemente “ suggeriscimi qualcos’altro da vedere ”, il sistema collega i puntini e calibra le proposte sui gusti che hai appena espresso. In più, sotto ogni risposta compaiono dei prompt suggeriti per continuare ad approfondire - ad esempio esplorando altri film dello stesso regista o titoli con un'atmosfera simile - senza dover nemmeno formulare una nuova domanda a voce.

Quante volte ti è capitato di mettere in pausa una serie o un evento sportivo per controllare sul telefono dove è stata girata una scena, quali altri film ha fatto il protagonista o come si intitola la canzone in sottofondo? Vision AI Companion elimina il bisogno di tenere lo smartphone a portata di mano mentre guardi la TV. Richiamando l'assistente durante la riproduzione, puoi fare domande dirette su ciò che stai guardando sullo schermo e ricevere schede informative chiare accompagnate da clip e video correlati su YouTube per approfondire subito. E se vuoi aggiornarti al volo prima di iniziare la serata, c'è “l’aggiornamento di oggi”: una funzione che sfrutta l'intelligenza artificiale per riassumere le principali notizie del giorno, le curiosità lifestyle e gli highlight sportivi, collegando ogni sintesi ai relativi video pronti da guardare.

Ma Vision AI Companion non serve solo a trovare film e serie TV: dalla schermata dedicata puoi anche dare sfogo alla creatività generando sfondi e immagini originali tramite IA generativa - perfetti da valorizzare su uno schermo antiriflesso insieme al Samsung Art Store - oppure chiedere aiuto direttamente al TV per orientarti tra le funzioni disponibili, il tutto protetto dalle policy Samsung sulla privacy e sulla gestione sicura dei dati domestici. Insomma, il telecomando smette di essere un tastierino con cui combattere e diventa semplicemente il tasto per iniziare la conversazione.

items.title: iRobot taglia i prezzi dei Roomba: con il Black Friday si risparmiano fino a 200 euro
items.summary: Dal 16 al 30 novembre su irobot.it nove Roomba costano meno, dai compatti che lavano i pavimenti ai Max con la base che fa quasi tutto da sola ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Oggi parte il Black Friday di iRobot, che fino al 30 novembre mette in offerta nove Roomba sul negozio online irobot.it. Il pezzo più atteso è il top di gamma: il Roomba Max 875 Combo con base AutoWash che ottiene uno sconto di ben 200 euro rispetto al prezzo degli ultimi 30 giorni. All'altro capo del listino il Roomba 115 Combo scende a soli 149 euro, e in mezzo c'è un robot per ogni casa e per ogni budget. La spedizione è gratuita e c'è sempre il reso entro 30 giorni.

I modelli sono tanti, ma si "leggono" bene se li si guarda per serie. Inoltre, salendo di prezzo e di caratteristiche il robot si prende in carico sempre più lavoro, fino a lasciarci soltanto il compito di cambiare un sacchetto una volta ogni pochi mesi.

Quasi tutti i Roomba in offerta sono Combo , cioè aspirano e lavano il pavimento nella stessa passata . Si orientano con un sensore laser LiDAR che disegna la mappa della casa, così il robot pulisce per file ordinate, sa dove è già passato e dall'app Roomba Home si scelgono le stanze da pulire.

A fare la differenza, salendo di prezzo, è soprattutto la base di ricarica. La AutoEmpty aspira lo sporco raccolto dal robot e lo chiude in un sacchetto che si cambia ogni tre mesi circa. La AutoWash fa lo stesso lavoro e in più lava e asciuga i panni o il rullo lavapavimenti , così il robot riparte ogni volta pulito.

L'ultimo numero da tenere d'occhio è la potenza di aspirazione, misurata in pascal (Pa): indica la depressione creata dal motore, e più è alta più sporco il robot tira su da tappeti e fughe.

Nel Roomba Max 875 Combo + AutoWash iRobot ha messo il massimo della tecnologia . Per il Black Friday costa 799 euro, contro un listino di 1.199 euro. È disponibile nero o bianco.

Aspira con 35.000 Pa, il valore più alto di tutta l'offerta. Quando sale su un tappeto, la tecnologia SealForce abbassa da sola il modulo di aspirazione e rende la pulizia del tappeto fino a tre volte più efficace. Il rullo e la spazzola laterale sono anti-groviglio, pensati per chi convive con capelli lunghi e peli di cani e gatti.

Per lavare usa il rullo PowerSpin Max , che gira a 300 giri al minuto e preme sul pavimento con 18 newton.

Sulle macchie più ostinate il robot passa prima con ThermaMist , una nebbia a ultrasuoni di acqua scaldata a 60 °C che pretratta lo sporco secco.

Con PerfectEdge il rullo si allunga lateralmente di 45 mm per arrivare fino al battiscopa, mentre DriLift lo solleva quando il robot riconosce un tappeto, che così resta asciutto.

La navigazione unisce il LiDAR ClearView Pro a PrecisionVision AI , una telecamera che riconosce gli oggetti sul pavimento, come cavi e scarpe, e li aggira invece di trascinarli . Il robot è alto 9,98 cm, quindi passa sotto molti divani, e supera soglie fino a 3,5 cm .

La base AutoWash chiude il cerchio. Lava il rullo con acqua a 80 °C, lo asciuga con aria a 55 °C perché non resti umido, dosa da sola il detergente e svuota la polvere dal robot . Prima di doverla toccare passano fino a 90 giorni.

Chi vuole un Max spendendo 200 euro in meno trova il Roomba Max 775 Combo + AutoWash a 599 euro, 100 in meno degli ultimi 30 giorni, nei colori nero o bianco.

Rispetto all'875 rinuncia a poco , e conserva tutte le carte della serie Max: 30.000 Pa, due spazzole in gomma anti-groviglio, Dirt Detect per riconoscere le zone più sporche e Carpet Boost, che alza la potenza sui tappeti.

Lava con il rullo PowerSpin , protetto da una copertura che tiene asciutti i tappeti quando il robot li attraversa, e vede gli ostacoli con la stessa PrecisionVision AI dell'875. La sua base lava il rullo a 75 °C, lo asciuga a 50 °C e svuota la polvere fino a tre mesi .

Per le case con molti tappeti, dove il lavaggio non serve, c'è il Roomba Max 715 Vac + AutoEmpty , un aspirapolvere puro con gli stessi 30.000 Pa , le due spazzole in gomma, Dirt Detect e Carpet Boost del 775. La base AutoEmpty lo svuota per un massimo di 90 giorni . Durante il Black Friday costa 379 euro.

Il rullo PowerSpin scende di prezzo con la serie Plus 600, che lo usa con acqua a 60 °C e 15 newton di pressione. Entrambi i modelli aspirano con 30.000 Pa, riconoscono gli ostacoli con PrecisionVision AI e sono alti 9,95 cm.

Il Roomba Plus 615 Combo con base Wash Only ha lo sconto più forte di tutta la campagna in percentuale, circa il 27%: costa 399 euro, 150 in meno degli ultimi 30 giorni. È la strada più economica per avere il rullo lavapavimenti. La base lava il rullo a 80 °C e lo asciuga , ma non svuota la polvere , che comunque finisce in un sacchetto da un litro dentro il robot e basta per circa un mese .

Il Roomba Plus 675 Combo + AutoWash costa 549 euro, nero o bianco, e la differenza con il 615 sta tutta nella base. Questa svuota anche la polvere, lava il rullo a 80 °C, lo asciuga con aria a 55 °C e dosa il detergente, per arrivare fino a 90 giorni senza interventi . Sul robot c'è PerfectEdge, già visto sull'875, e una spazzola con un meccanismo taglia-peli che li accorcia mentre gira; in questo non resta avvolta e non c'è da liberarla con le forbici.

La serie Plus 400 e 500 è quella che entra dove gli altri restano fuori. Il 415 e il 575 sono alti appena 8,35 cm (il 21% in meno del Roomba Plus 505 della generazione precedente), e passano sotto letti, divani e mobili bassi dove la polvere si accumula indisturbata. Lavano con due panni rotanti DualClean da 200 giri al minuto, che si sollevano di 10 mm quando il robot riconosce un tappeto . Entrambi hanno la base AutoWash e sono disponibili in nero o bianco.

Il Roomba Plus 415 Combo + AutoWash scende a 299 euro. Aspira con 20.000 Pa e con SmartScrub preme di più sul pavimento per staccare le macchie secche. La base lava e asciuga i panni con aria calda, così non restano umidi fino al giro successivo .

Il Roomba Plus 575 Combo + AutoWash è l'occasione della fascia media: per il periodo promo costa 379 euro. Aspira con 25.000 Pa e porta su un robot così sottile la navigazione ClearView Pro con PrecisionVision AI, la stessa dei Max. La base lava i panni con acqua fino a 75 °C e poi li asciuga con aria calda.

Per cominciare a delegare la pulizia di casa basta il Roomba 115 Combo , che durante il Black Friday costa solo 149 euro, nero o bianco.

Ha la stessa navigazione laser dei modelli superiori , aspira con 15.000 Pa e lava con un panno in microfibra che si stacca e si lava.

È alto 9,2 cm e con una carica copre fino a 84 metri quadrati, cioè un appartamento di medie dimensioni.

Con 30 euro in più si smette anche di svuotarlo. Infatti, il Roomba 115 Combo + AutoEmpty costa 179 euro, ed è il modo più economico per avere un robot che si svuota da solo. La base raccoglie lo sporco in un sacchetto AllergenLock da 2,5 litri, che trattiene il 99% di pollini e muffe e dura circa tre mesi .

items.title: Il Black Friday Tineco arriva prima. Sconti fino a 250 euro su aspirapolvere e lavapavimenti
items.summary: Cinque prodotti Tineco in promozione fino al 30 novembre, sia su Amazon sia sullo store online. Per il Black Friday inizia a pulire meno e a vivere meglio ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Il Black Friday può essere l'occasione per automatizzare o almeno rendere meno faticose alcune delle attività domestiche che si ripetono ogni giorno. È il principio attorno al quale Tineco, parte del Gruppo ECOVACS, ha costruito la propria selezione di offerte per il Black Friday: cinque prodotti che affrontano esigenze differenti, dalla pulizia quotidiana dei pavimenti alle macchie più difficili, passando per peli di animali, tappeti e tessuti.

Con gli sconti per il Black Friday, validi sia su Amazon sia sullo store online di Tineco, si risparmia fino a 250 euro . Inoltre, acquistando su Amazon è previsto un ulteriore sconto del 6% sul prezzo promozionale Black Friday utilizzando il codice TINECOBFIT in fase dei checkout .

La selezione scelta da Tineco riflette il concetto "Clean Less, Live More" del marchio: usare sensori, automazione, autopulizia e soluzioni meccaniche studiate per ridurre non soltanto il lavoro durante la pulizia, ma anche quello necessario subito dopo.

Dalla possibilità di reclinare a 180° il dispositivo per facilitare il passaggio sotto ai mobili più bassi fino al lavaggio e all’asciugatura automatizzati. Così da passare meno tempo a pulire e più tempo a vivere.

FLOOR ONE S9 Artist Steam Pro è la proposta più completa tra quelle coinvolte nella promozione e nasce per unire in un unico dispositivo aspirazione, lavaggio e trattamento con vapore ad alta temperatura. Ciò per evitare di dover affrontare separatamente polvere, sporco umido e macchie più difficili. Il sistema intelligente, infatti, rileva le condizioni della superficie e modifica automaticamente il funzionamento della lavapavimenti, adattando l'intervento allo sporco incontrato durante il passaggio.

Il vapore aggiunge un'azione specifica quando acqua e aspirazione da sole non sono sufficienti, per esempio nel caso di residui secchi o sporco più aderente al pavimento.

Ma una parte importante del lavoro viene automatizzata anche quando si finisce di pulire. La tecnologia FlashDry gestisce un ciclo di pulizia e asciugatura del rullo , riducendo gli interventi necessari prima di riporre il dispositivo. È disponibile anche un’asciugatura silenziosa che lavora a meno di 45 dB.

La FLOOR ONE S9 Artist Steam Pro Include anche uno schermo facile da avere sempre sott’occhio per conoscere in un attimo l’autonomia residua e la modalità di pulizia selezionata. Mentre il sistema SmoothDrive garantisce una propulsione a 360° e facilita la spinta in ogni direzione, così da non gravare sul polso e ridurre lo sforzo. L’autonomia arriva fino a 90 minuti.

Per il Black Friday, FLOOR ONE S9 Artist Steam Pro è in sconto a 629 euro anziché 849 euro sia su Amazon sia sullo store online di Tineco .

Poco più in basso nella gamma si trova FLOOR ONE S9 Artist Boost Steam. Anche in questo caso il vapore svolge un ruolo da protagonista, ma l’impostazione è più orientata alla rapidità di intervento.

La BoostSteam Technology rende disponibile il getto di vapore in circa 20 secondi alla prima attivazione e in circa 5 secondi per le erogazioni successive. Il vapore può raggiungere una temperatura di 230 °C e viene utilizzato per intervenire su residui secchi e macchie particolarmente ostinate.

A questa azione si affianca la ReverseScrub Technology. La spazzola può ruotare in senso inverso per aumentare l'azione meccanica sul pavimento e raggiungere meglio anche le fughe tra le piastrelle.

L’aspirazione, invece, arriva fino a 25.000 Pa e permette di raccogliere anche lo sporco umido durante il passaggio. Per raggiungere le aree normalmente più difficili c'è il design HyperStretch: la lavapavimenti può reclinarsi fino a 180 gradi e passare così sotto letti, divani e mobili bassi senza obbligare a spostarli. Inoltre, garantisce fino a 60 minuti di autonomia.

Il prezzo di listino di FLOOR ONE S9 Artist Boost Steam è di 699 euro; durante il Black Friday scende a 579,99 euro sia su Amazon sia sul sito ufficiale di Tineco .

FLOOR ONE S7 Stretch Ultra rinuncia al vapore e si concentra, invece, sulla pulizia quotidiana combinando aspirazione e lavaggio in un unico passaggio. Una delle caratteristiche principali è il sistema MHCBS di Tineco, progettato per alimentare continuamente il rullo con acqua pulita e separare quella sporca raccolta durante il passaggio. Il principio è quello di continuare a lavare il pavimento utilizzando un rullo mantenuto pulito durante il funzionamento, anziché trascinare progressivamente lo sporco già raccolto.

Inoltre, per le case nelle quali capelli e peli rappresentano una presenza quotidiana c'è il sistema DualBlock Anti-Tangle, studiato per ridurre la formazione di grovigli attorno al rullo e quindi anche la manutenzione manuale.

La parola "Stretch" anticipa un'altra delle sue caratteristiche distintive: il corpo può reclinarsi completamente fino a 180 gradi, così da lavorare anche sotto mobili e altri elementi bassi senza costringere chi la utilizza a fermarsi o cambiare strumento. In questo modo può passare sotto a mobili alti fino a 13 cm . La posizione reclinata non compromette la qualità della pulizia grazie al sistema di separazione delle acque reflue in tre camere distinte.

È anche uno dei prodotti sui quali il Black Friday incide maggiormente: FLOOR ONE S7 Stretch Ultra passa da un prezzo di listino di 499 euro a 249,99 euro. Lo sconto è attivo sia su Amazon sia sullo store online di Tineco .

Non tutto lo sporco si trova sui pavimenti duri. CARPET ONE Spot DualHeat è pensato proprio per le superfici sulle quali una normale lavapavimenti non può intervenire. Si pensi a tappeti, divani, scale rivestite e sedili o tessuti dell’automobile.

Il sistema combina acqua calda fino a 70 °C e vapore fino a 100 °C . Sono disponibili quattro livelli di pulizia, così da poter calibrare l'intervento in funzione del problema: dallo schizzo appena avvenuto fino allo sporco che ha avuto più tempo per aderire alle fibre.

L'aspirazione arriva fino a 17.000 Pa ed è utilizzata per recuperare l'acqua sporca e i residui dopo il trattamento. Un aspetto particolarmente importante quando si lavano i tessuti è poi il tempo necessario perché tornino utilizzabili: per questo Tineco integra FlipDry, con due modalità di asciugatura pensate proprio per accelerare questa fase. Con questo sistema, il CARPET ONE Spot DualHeat usa l’aria calda fino a 70 °C e un flusso d’aria di 4,2 m/s per asciugare più in fretta. Oppure, in caso di tessuti sensibili al calore, come tappeti in lana e biancheria in cotone, si può optare per un’asciugatura più delicata.

CARPET ONE Spot DualHeat ha un prezzo di listino di 249 euro e per il Black Friday viene proposto a 209 euro. La promozione è disponibile sia su Amazon sia sul sito di Tineco .

PURE ONE S50 Pro Pet è il prodotto più accessibile della selezione Black Friday, ma anche quello con un compito molto specifico: semplificare la pulizia quotidiana nelle abitazioni in cui vivono cani e gatti. In queste case il problema non è necessariamente lo sporco più difficile, quanto la sua frequenza. Peli, capelli e polvere ricompaiono continuamente e richiedono quindi uno strumento che possa essere utilizzato rapidamente senza trasformare ogni passaggio in una sessione di pulizia completa.

Per questo PURE ONE S50 Pro Pet utilizza una spazzola anti-groviglio progettata per raccogliere capelli e peli limitandone l'accumulo sulla spazzola stessa. Una volta finito, anche lo svuotamento del contenitore avviene con un solo gesto.

Prima ancora di aspirare, però, bisogna riuscire a vedere lo sporco. Il faro verde grandangolare copre un angolo di 120 gradi e mette in evidenza particelle fino a 0,02 mm, comprese quelle che possono risultare poco visibili a occhio nudo sul pavimento.

Il sensore iLoop, invece, lavora durante l'aspirazione: rileva quanto sporco è presente e modifica automaticamente la potenza, evitando di dover regolare continuamente il dispositivo a mano e contribuendo a gestire meglio la carica disponibile. L'autonomia dichiarata arriva fino a 90 minuti , mentre il design reclinabile aiuta a passare sotto mobili e arredi bassi, dove peli e polvere tendono facilmente ad accumularsi.

PURE ONE S50 Pro Pet è in promozione su Amazon e sullo store online di Tineco fino al 30 novembre a 199 euro, rispetto al prezzo precedente di 299 euro

items.title: Europe ready for talks with Russia on ending war in Ukraine, leaders say
items.summary: European allies of Ukraine say they have a "united" negotiating position at a summit in Berlin.
items.content:
European leaders have said they are ready for negotiations with Russia on ending the war in Ukraine, in a strong show of support for Kyiv.

"Europe has a clear and consistent and united negotiating position," UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said, while German Chancellor Friedrich Merz stressed that Moscow's "maximalist demands are not realistic".

They were speaking at Berlin's summit of Ukraine's allies known as the Coalition of the Willing.

Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner, one of the two US envoys who were in Berlin, said the US president wanted to make a deal with Moscow "with Europe by his side". Russia's Vladimir Putin has so far rejected any European role in the US-led peace talks.

Trump had earlier held historic trilateral talks in Shenzhen , south-eastern China, with Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping and later dialled into the Berlin summit from Air Force One.

In a lengthy press conference following his talks with Trump and Xi, Putin addressed the question of multilateral peace talks, saying the Americans were "insistently" asking Russia to allow the Europeans to take part.

Putin claimed Russia was not against the idea but said Moscow wanted to clarify "what Europe will bring to these talks".

"That is why, through diplomatic channels, we have invited the Europeans to come to Moscow in order to determine their positions. And after that, we will decide in what format we will continue the dialogue with Ukraine."

But Putin also said that "every day" Russia heard that European leaders were talking about war coming in 2030. "But we are not planning to attack anyone... Is that normal? I do not think so," he said. Still, Putin added, Russia understood that "discussing issues linked to security in Europe is pointless without the Europeans".

Jared Kushner told reporters that the US president had come away from Shenzhen believing that "peace is achievable".

Striking an upbeat note, Kushner said that the Russians were willing to trust the instinct of the US envoys "on our behalf" that the Europeans should be at the table and that Moscow was now "comfortable" with Ukraine having security guarantees based on the idea enshrined in Nato's Article Five that requires allies to come to a country's defence if it comes under attack.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, who also was at the summit in Germany's capital, has long sought a guarantee equivalent to Nato's collective defence clause, and there has been little indication that Putin would accept that kind of condition.

Russia rejects outright the idea of Ukrainian membership of Nato, but reports say US negotiators have mulled the idea of giving Kyiv Article Five-style guarantees without being part of the Western defensive alliance if it agrees to painful territorial concessions.

Zelensky and the three European leaders – Merz, Burnham and French President Emmanuel Macron – were not as upbeat as Kushner, and the Ukrainian president made clear that the Russian president had spurned every proposal so far: "Putin has always said no."

The German chancellor was equally sceptical, although he said with US involvement the chance of peace was increasing. Europe was willing to enter "serious discussions on European security" with Russia, he explained, "as long as it's matched with a serious discussion and only first a peace agreement with Ukraine".

"These talks have to begin, and we will accept if conditions are acceptable for Europe and Ukraine," said Merz.

He also said any attempts to divide Europe into spheres of influence run by major powers was unacceptable, amid concerns on the continent that this issue may have been on the agenda at the trilateral talks in Shenzhen.

Analysis: Trilateral summit high on spectacle, short on substance

"A 'Yalta format' will not bring peace," Merz said, referring to the post-World War Two agreement between the US, the USSR and Britain in 1945.

He also sought to downplay the Shenzhen summit as above all "a photo opportunity."

"The US understands that there can be no peace without us. We, in turn, know that with the United States by our side, the prospects for peace increase," Merz added.

Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk also took exception to Trump's description of Putin as a "friend" at the Shenzhen summit, saying: "Mr Putin is not our friend and will never be."

Meanwhile, Macron urged Ukraine's allies to do the "maximum" to deliver the much-needed air defence systems Kyiv needed to repel deadly Russian attacks.

The French leader also urged the allies to "reopen the question" of Ukraine's membership in Nato.

There have been mixed messages from Moscow on European participation to the talks. Last week, following a visit to Moscow, the US envoys, Steve Witkoff and Kushner, appeared certain that Europe would soon have a seat at the negotiating table.

But the Russians were more circumspect and this week Putin's aide Yury Ushakov said a "great deal" would have to be done before the format could be expanded, suggesting that several more rounds of discussions would have to be held before any four-sided talks could take place.

Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

While Russia has engaged with several rounds of talks over the last year, little in Moscow's rhetoric or actions suggests that the Kremlin is considering scaling down its war on Ukraine.

It continues to pound Kyiv's energy infrastructure to cripple it as winter takes hold, increasing numbers of civilian casualties are being recorded across the country, and Kremlin officials have not budged from Russia's demands for Ukrainian sovereign territory.

As delegations were meeting in China and Germany on Thursday, several buildings in Kyiv's historic centre came under attack from drones. One person was killed in a strike on a residential building in the Podilskyi neighbourhood, while the Dutch and Austrian embassies as well as Saint Volodymyr's Cathedral reported damage.

And Putin also vowed that Moscow's response to a Ukrainian strike on the Crimean Bridge linking Russia with occupied Crimea would be "considerably more painful" than what Kyiv had achieved.

He also said he had discussed a "possible ceasefire in a number of areas" but had decided against it after the attack on the bridge.

Still, Putin claimed to be "interested" in ending the war and was ready to make compromises, while Ukraine and Europe were not.

"I assure you, we have no desire at all to continue this armed conflict," Putin said, despite the fact that Russia has in recent months intensified its attacks on Ukraine's critical infrastructure as cold winter approaches.

Kyiv and its European allies say that – in the absence of any major success on the vast front line – the Kremlin leader is seeking to break Ukrainian resistance by leaving millions of civilians without electricity and water supply.

items.title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back
items.summary: Shark Tank's Kevin O'Leary is among the big investors looking to Canada as a data centre development destination, while his US project faces local opposition.
items.content:
As Americans have grown increasingly sour on artificial intelligence (AI) data centre development, Canada's industry leaders are sensing an opportunity.

"Data centres in Canada looking pretty appealing right now," Lucy Hargreaves, CEO of non-profit policy group Build Canada, wrote on X the day after American voters passed 40 of 41 local ballot initiatives aimed at limiting or preventing data centre development in this month's midterm elections.

While the number of proposed AI data centres in the US dwarfs that of its northern neighbour, in recent months Canada is being increasingly pitched as a hub for these so-called "hyperscale" projects.

Those in favour argue that Canada's abundant land, natural gas and cold climate make it uniquely positioned to address some of the problems facing US AI infrastructure, from data centres' proximity to populated areas to noise pollution and strain on electricity grids.

"Some of the capital that would have been deployed to build data centres in the US is now more available for Canada," Hargreaves told the BBC in an interview.

"The question really is whether or not we want to go for that."

Unlike in the US, pushback to these projects in Canada has been muted - at least so far. Many are going ahead without significant disruptions, and legislators have openly embraced them without major political consequences.

At the heart of Canada's AI data centre boom is Alberta, where 90% of all currently proposed sites are set to be built.

The western Canadian province, rich with natural gas deposits, has pitched itself as "North America's destination of choice" for AI data centres, including by offering a "concierge" service for investors to help build these projects at "unparalleled speed".

One of those investors is Kevin O'Leary, the Canadian businessman, TV personality and an ally of Donald Trump, who announced plans this year to build two large AI data centres - one in Alberta and one in the US state of Utah.

His planned sites, both named Wonder Valley, are being received in very different ways on either side of the border.

Residents in Utah have organised a fierce opposition campaign. , external The pushback led outgoing state senator Stuart Adams to demand in June that O'Leary scale down the project by 75% , external , from 40,000 to 13,000 acres.

Financing for the Utah Wonder Valley data centre is still underway, and it is unclear when - and if - shovels will hit the ground on the project.

The proposed 7,000-acre, 7.5-gigawatt Alberta Wonder Valley project, meanwhile, has received strong backing from both the provincial government and the local municipality.

The project is billed as "off-grid" , external , relying on its own power system fuelled by natural gas sourced from the region. In April, the Alberta government exempted the project from an environmental impact assessment , external , arguing it was unnecessary, though it will still need to obtain permits prior to construction.

The project was met with only limited opposition at a local town hall earlier this year. One resident, Dan Harms, told Bloomberg in June , external that he saw the economic benefits of the Wonder Valley data centre and that it was being built "out in the middle of nowhere".

In an interview with BBC News, Reeve Ryan Ratzlaf, of Greenview Municipality in north-western Alberta, said the project was the "perfect fit" for his rural community, which had been looking for an industrial tenant to fill a resource-rich parcel of land for 13 years.

Some community members have expressed concern about the amount of water needed to cool the proposed site annually, which is projected to be six million cubic metres, or about the size of 2,400 Olympic-size swimming pools.

Ratzlaf argued the amount was a drop compared to the annual flow of the nearby Smoky River, from which the centre would pull water. More broadly, he said he believed that economic benefits to the region outweighed potential risks.

"It's a giant warehouse with computer equipment inside," he said, arguing that it was less risky than petrochemical plants that could have been built in its place.

Speaking to BBC News, the CEO overseeing both O'Leary projects, Paul Palandjian, said the two were proceeding at an "equal" pace.

He acknowledged it had become more of a "hot topic" in the US than in Alberta. But there are signs public anger towards AI data centres in Alberta has grown in recent months.

Recent public information sessions on provincial AI data centre plans were attended by some furious residents.

"If no one wants this, why are you pushing forward with this?" one resident asked in an August town hall reported on by the Canadian Press , external , held shortly after Alberta announced that Meta would build a C$13bn ($9bn; £6.8bn) AI data centre in the province.

Sturgeon Lake Cree Nation has also recently sued the government over its decision to override the environmental assessment for O'Leary's Wonder Valley data centre, labelling it "irrational" in court filings.

This week, the Alberta government proposed legislation that would put restrictions on where data centres could be built in a bid to ease some concerns.

There are also signs that public cooperation may be fading elsewhere in the country.

On Saturday, hundreds of protesters gathered in Canada's Atlantic province of Nova Scotia against a proposed AI data centre , external that will be used by technology giant Anthropic.

But experts say the US backlash offers a cautionary tale for Canada as it tries to capitalise on the AI boom.

"AI is generally not very popular. This is both true in Canada and the United States," noted Sean Mullin, a senior fellow at the University of Toronto and former adviser to Canada's prime minister on the national sovereign AI compute strategy.

"I think we could experience some of the same backlashes if we're not thoughtful about it," he said.

The Carney government, which has made reducing Canada's reliance on the US a priority, has framed the development of AI data centres as a matter of national security and sovereignty. It has projected that Canada needs to expand its computing capacity 16-fold over the next four years to meet domestic demand.

Alberta is defending its data centre plans by saying they will create jobs and generate revenue, and that sites will be developed "responsibly".

In Ontario, Premier Doug Ford has said that his province needs to move "full steam ahead" with building data centres.

Mullin said one reason the backlash had been less severe in Canada was simply due to scope and timing.

"There has been less of these projects happening, and as a result, they've attracted less attention," he said.

Canada has released some high-level guidance on data centre development, which has been co-signed by Anthropic, Meta and other big AI players. It calls on data centres to pay for electricity costs, minimise water use and create long-term benefits for the regions they are in.

If politicians don't tread carefully, Bek MacIntosh, an Alberta resident who has fought a proposed hyperscale data centre in her community, said she believed public discontent could translate into angry votes, like those seen in the US.

MacIntosh successfully halted a data centre in Olds, Alberta, , external over concerns with its scale, scope and proximity to her home. Even after her eight-month battle, she said she was not opposed to all AI infrastructure and believed Canada had the resources and landscape to build them responsibly.

But she fears Alberta has opened the door to "the most reckless of reckless developers", and warned that voters might have a "knee-jerk reaction" if provinces don't take care to develop AI data centres responsibly.

"And I don't think any political party in Canada is prepared for it."

'We all need data, but do we need the largest data centre in Europe here?'

Did a data centre revolt affect the US midterm election results?

items.title: 'I tell my son it's just fireworks': Life inside Yemeni city besieged by Houthis
items.summary: Orla Guerin speaks to seven people trapped in the key city of Taiz, cut off from the outside world for weeks.
items.content:
In the Yemeni city of Taiz, ringed by jagged mountains and Houthi rebel fighters, Ashwaq has only one way to try to soothe her frightened child - lie.

"When my 11-year-old son hears a loud sound, I tell him, 'Don't be afraid, it's just fireworks'," she says. "I don't want him to panic, but deep down I know he is old enough to understand what is happening around him. He has lived through war for most of his life."

Taiz has long been a prize - and a front line - in Yemen's civil war.

Houthi forces tightened their grip last month, fully encircling the government-controlled city, and the population - estimated to be between 600,000 and 1 million.

Since then, Yemen's third-largest city has been cut off from the world, and its residents have been largely unheard. We reached seven people inside the city who mapped out the anatomy of the siege.

They gave detailed accounts of the Houthis' death grip on Taiz. Only a minimal amount of food can get in. Prices for staples like rice, sugar and cooking oil have doubled or even trebled. Essential supplies, like medicine, water and fuel, are dwindling.

On streets that used to hum with traffic and background chatter, a silence has fallen. Schools are closed and restaurants are shuttered. Suffering is being heaped on suffering. Piles of rubbish are trapped inside the city, alongside the people. When residents try to get rid of it by burning it, there is a toxic smoke. Even the air is now a Houthi weapon.

From positions on the hills, rebel fighters - and snipers - can wage war on the city below.

Estimates for the death toll vary widely. At the Office for Siege Affairs, a local government department, they say 148 civilians have been killed by Houthi attacks since August.

Some of those we contacted in Taiz do not want to be identified because they fear for their safety. Many in the city are reluctant to even speak on the phone because the Houthis control key mobile carriers.

"Sometimes it feels like the city has become a huge prison," says Ashwaq, a teacher and mother of three, who only wanted her first name to be used. She yearns for the old Taiz.

"It used to be a lively city," she says. "People loved life, worked hard, visited one another, and had hopes for the future, despite all the difficulties. Now, we hardly go out anymore. The [Houthi] shelling can happen any time, and sniper fire near the front lines makes even a short trip dangerous."

"I worry about them every single day, every hour, and honestly every minute," she says.

War is not new to Taiz. The strategic city is the gateway to Aden - the temporary seat of the internationally recognised government - and to southern Yemen.

Houthi rebels - backed by Iran - reached the outskirts of Taiz in 2015, cutting off roads, and laying siege from three sides. A year earlier, they had seized Yemen's capital, Sanaa.

More than a decade on, the government, which is weak and fractured, has been unable to reclaim the capital and much of north-western Yemen. That's despite the backing of Saudi Arabia, and its air strikes.

In recent months, the conflict has flared up and expanded after a four-year lull. The Houthis made a lightning advance, taking territory from the government, and striking Saudi Arabia with missiles and drones.

A long-running civil war has become a threat to regional stability.

An emergency room doctor, whom we are calling Yaser, bears witness to that.

Among the war wounded recently brought to his hospital were four children, shot by Houthi snipers. They usually aim for the head and chest, he tells us. Two of the four children died.

The hardest thing he faces, as a father himself, is treating wounded children. "I have to rise to the responsibility, compose myself and support the families," he says. "It's a difficult situation that I cannot even put into words, when I see a father looking at his badly wounded child right in front of him."

Most of the injured are victims of shelling. Reaching the hospital can be an ordeal. Some families have to walk for hours from outlying areas.

They arrive exhausted, like the doctors who will treat them, and who are struggling with "everything", says Yaser. Even sterilising fluid for surgical instruments is in short supply.

He tells us the hospital is running on empty, and can carry on for two more weeks, "maybe".

"Funerals heading to the cemeteries have become the defining scene in Taiz, around the clock," says Taiz's Governor, Nabil Shamsan.

"The people of Taiz are losing their lives due to supply shortages, lack of food, and loss of income," he says. "Every single day, we bury dozens of Taiz residents."

He remains inside the city, and inside the siege. "I live among my people," he says.

On a video call, he looks weary but delivers a lengthy chronicle of a city being starved of oxygen - literally.

He tells us that hospitals have lost 70% of their capacity, and 120 health centres have closed. Diseases are spreading, neonatal deaths have increased, and malnutrition is surging. Hundreds of kidney patients are not getting dialysis because they can't get to hospitals or because fuel is short when they do.

The Houthi leader, Abdul Malik al-Houthi, has denied Taiz is besieged. Late last month, he claimed that routes remained open for food, medicine and humanitarian aid.

That is denied by the government, residents of Taiz, aid agencies and the United Nations.

What's at stake in the battle for the city is more than territory, says Shamsan.

He says the Houthis - who mostly follow a branch of Shia Islam - want to change the character of this predominantly Sunni city, long known as a seat of learning and a bastion of resistance.

"Everyone knows that Taiz is a hub of culture, a city characterised by freedom, political pluralism and all forms of civic life," he says. In sharp contrast, he says, the Houthis aim to impose their strict religious doctrine and drag the city "back to the dark ages".

Whatever the pressure on the city and its people, the governor insists the Houthis will never win.

They are defending their city, alongside relatives, friends, neighbours, and five brigades of pro-government troops, who can't do the job on their own.

They don't have heavy weapons or enough numbers for the expanding front line.

Training camps have sprung up for volunteers, but the lessons can be as brief as a day or two before they are sent to join the fight.

Akram (not his real name) is already a veteran. He's 31, with a child on the way.

When Taiz was fully encircled before, in 2015, he broke away from his studies and took up arms. In that round of fighting, the Houthis gained control of his district on the outskirts, and he was uprooted. He hasn't seen his old home since then.

Last month, when Taiz was completely cut off once again, he bought a rifle, paying about $1,200 (£910) for a Chinese version of a Kalashnikov. It used to cost less than half that sum.

"This time the Houthis have new technology and new missiles," he says. "They can wage a war in the air with drones. We fear the death of our families and our civilians, and ourselves."

He has already lost four friends in the past month, who left behind wives and children.

But Akram, and many others, see defending Taiz as their duty. He says that "all the sons of Taiz" will fight the Houthis "and their extremism".

The armed group is currently designated as a foreign terrorist organisation by the US (which has gone back and forth on the issue) but not by the UK or the European Union.

"They say God gave them the right to rule everyone in Yemen. We don't accept that," says Akram. "We live in freedom. We cannot surrender; we cannot leave. We cannot breathe without our city."

But it can be suffocating inside Taiz, where nightfall brings no rest.

"Every night we have bombing and shelling," says Ahmad Al-Basha, a photographer. "I think the Houthis prefer to fight at night. Maybe they don't want us and our children to sleep inside our homes."

The people of Taiz feel let down, he tells us, by their government and by the international community. "We feel frustrated and sad," he says, "because we don't see any move to help us."

Many believe the Houthis will keep a chokehold on Taiz from the outside, and exert significant control over the city without trying to enter it.

Ahmad believes it won't come to that but fears the worst if it does.

"Maybe they will clean Taiz of any resistance, kill people and settle scores with anyone who is against them," he says.

His greatest concern is for his children, who cannot escape the sounds of war.

"I tell them it's a party," he says, "and if it's really loud, I say it's a big party."

As Taiz endures bombing, shelling, and a sense of abandonment laced with growing hunger, Ashwaq has a parent's plea for the international community.

"Please don't forget Taiz," she says. "We are ordinary families. We want our children to study, play and dream like other children around the world. We are not just numbers in news reports."

On Yemen's desert battlefield, a war with global consequences is being waged

Newborn twins fight for survival as conflict fuels Yemen's hunger crisis
